After that, linear layer is served as a feature extraction layer and these features are further processed into classification with SVM classifier to classify the reviews into binary labels as positive and negative reviews. From the results, the proposed distilBERT-SVM achieved better results than the existing systems in terms of accuracy, precision, recall and Fl-score of 98.2%, 98.5%, 92.3% and 94.5% respectively.

articleTitle: Marine Safety Enhancement through Oil Spill Detection Using U-Net Architecture
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Integrated Intelligence and Communication Systems (ICIICS)
abstract: Oil spills pose a significant danger to marine ecosystems, coastal inhabitants, and various economic activities. Early identification is crucial, as the rates of spread and impact increase, making containment more challenging. This research investigates the application of the U-Net architecture for oil spill detection. The component called skip connections, along with the U-Net encoder-decoder structure, enables precise location and segmentation of oil spills, which are typically complex and have irregular shapes, from SAR imagery. Other approaches rely on manual analysis, which is time-consuming and relatively inaccurate. By applying U-Net as a deep learning method, our approach achieved 96% accuracy in identifying oil-contaminated areas, proving to be more efficient compared to traditional methods. This increase in efficacy enhances countermeasures, response times, and resource deployment due to the technology's precise detection capabilities, ultimately benefiting marine conservation efforts.

articleTitle: RNNs and LSTMs Based Synchronization Analysis of Indian Stock Market
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Integrated Intelligence and Communication Systems (ICIICS)
abstract: By use of recurrence plots (RP) and cross recurrence quantification analysis (CRQA) model nonlinear correlation in stocks used Cross Recurrence Plot (CRP) data converted into a time-series data because RNN and LSTM can be used in this research which can be used for both regression and classification in stock market price prediction. RNN and LSTM model used as compare to other models because it is better for sequential data and non-linear dynamics, and it predicts stock prices with high accuracy. Using given dataset which contain 20 highly capitalized Indian market stocks spanning 21 years this model got highest accuracy of 0.98 and F1 score of 0.83 as compare to existing model used till now in this work, results method can accurately forecast stock price synchronization, providing useful information for creating trading plans and risk management instruments.

articleTitle: Landslide Detection and Early Warning System Using Extended Kalman Filter with Convolutional Neural Networks Based Long Short-Term Memory
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Integrated Intelligence and Communication Systems (ICIICS)
abstract: Nowadays, landslides are a major risk to human life and causing devastating consequences. and economic stability by resulting substantial losses annually. The effective landslide risk management relies on timely recognition of spatial changes in patterns. patterns. Traditional approaches for developing the warning system for landslide had faced challenges which includes linearity assumption and difficulty in handling non-stationary data. Therefore, this paper proposes Extended Kalman Filter-Convolutional Neural Networks-Long Short-Term Memory (EKF-CNN-LSTM) for landslide detection and early warning system. Initially, the data is collected from Fast Deploying Monitoring System (FDMS) which consists of ad-hoc router, sensors related to landslides. Then, the data is preprocessed by using Fast Fourier Transform (FFT), which effectively filtered out noise and irrelevant frequency components by improving signal quality. After that, model is trained by proposed EKF-CNN-LSTM which generated real time prediction, early warnings of potential landslides. Finally, the early warnings are predicted and give output as “no warning” or “warning,” by enabling the timely interventions. By integrating these technologies into landslide monitoring and EWS, enhanced the prediction accuracy and provided timely warnings. The proposed EKF-CNN-LSTM succeeded with high results including accuracy (0.943), precision (0.832), recall (0.786), F1-score (0.798) and MCC (0.743) when compared with existing ResNet101.

articleTitle: Optimizing Deep Convolutional Neural Networks with Progressive Unfreezing for Enhanced Sports Activity Recognition
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Integrated Intelligence and Communication Systems (ICIICS)
abstract: This study presents a methodology to enhance sports activity recognition using advanced deep Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs). The objective is to fine-tune CNN architectures for accurate classification of various sports activities from image data. A systematic preprocessing pipeline employs data augmentation techniques-such as random rotations and horizontal flipping-alongside normalization and resizing for consistent training. This study explores several CNN architectures, including EfficientNetB0, ResNet50, EfficientNetB3, Xception, and EfficientNetB7, using a progressive unfreezing approach. The proposed appraoch achieved an impressive accuracy of 87.00% with EfficientNetB0 on the benchmark Clever dataset. This research contributes to deep learning methodologies in sports classification, showcasing the effectiveness of progressive unfreezing to improve accuracy and encouraging further exploration of diverse sports activities.

articleTitle: An Optimized Field Programmable Gate Array Based Noise Reduction Techniques for Fetal Electrocardiogram Signal Processing
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Integrated Intelligence and Communication Systems (ICIICS)
abstract: Analyzing fetal electrocardiogram (FECG) signals is essential for identifying fetal cardiac disorders early on, although noise interference is still a problem. Conventional signal processing techniques can produce conflicting findings. With an emphasis on three important noise reduction methods the Kalman Filter, Discrete wavelet transform, and Finite impulse response this study evaluates the performance of the PYNQZ2 and NEXYS A 7 Field Programmable Gate Array (FPGA) boards in real-time FECG signal monitoring. With a mean squared error of 0.58% and a signal-to-noise ratio of 31.1 dB, the Kalman Filter fared better than the other filters, especially when it came to lowering dynamic noise in real-time applications. Furthermore, the PYNQ Z2 was outperformed by the NEXYS A7 board at processing FECG signals efficiently. effectively. By providing insights into the best noise reduction strategies and improving the accuracy of FECG monitoring in biomedical applications, this comparative analysis advances FPGA-based signal processing systems.

articleTitle: Efficient Hardware Accelerator Design for AES Encryption Using High-Level Synthesis Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Integrated Intelligence and Communication Systems (ICIICS)
abstract: In this work, we present the design and implementation of a hardware accelerator for AES encryption and decryption using AMD Vitis HLS and Xilinx Vivado. The primary objective of this work is to maximize the throughput, with optimizations focusing on resource utilization and power consumption. We detail the design methodology, provide an in-depth analysis of resource utilization, and compare our results with existing AES hardware accelerators. The hardware accelerator has been deployed on a PYNQ-Z2 FPGA board, achieving a throughput of 20.8 Gbps at 650 MHz, Total power consumption of 1.418W. The results show significant performance improvements, demonstrating the viability of high-level synthesis (HLS) for cryptographic applications on FPGAs.

articleTitle: Trustworthy IoT Infrastructures: Privacy-Preserving Federated Learning with Efficient Secure Aggregation for Cybersecurity
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Integrated Intelligence and Communication Systems (ICIICS)
abstract: Smart gadgets have become ubiquitous due to the fast development of the Internet of Things (IoT). In an effort to recover the precision and excellence of their services, service providers are aggressively gathering massive amounts of customer data to train machine learning models. This technique, however, has caused people to worry about the security of their personal information. Most importantly, this is accomplished without directly transmitting data to a central server, which greatly reduces the risks of privacy breaches. Users' data stays local in federated learning because machine learning algorithms operate locally, transmitting back only the local classical to the central server. New studies show, however, that local models incorporate user data privacy considerations as well. Additionally, training with existing privacy-preserving secure aggregation approaches requires extremely expensive computing resources or provides inadequate accuracy. Our work presents a secure and efficient aggregation scheme for privacy-preserving federated learning that minimises computational costs. This scheme is well-suited for low-powered Internet of Things devices because it is resilient and fault-tolerant, enabling users to join or leave the system on the fly without negatively impacting the federated learning process or causing abnormal termination. Combining the best features of both methods, this research employed a novel attack classification model based on a hybrid random forest and a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN). Using the CICIoT2023 dataset, we validate the suggested approach and show that it improves the security of IoT ecosystems. Lightweight, trust-managing, and privacy-preserving Internet of Things (IoT) infrastructures are urgently needed, and this research helps to meet that demand.-maintaining answers while cybersecurity threats evolve. Integrating private data into an IoT setting, the suggested system demonstrates trustworthiness.

articleTitle: Self-Attention Mechanism and Balanced Loss Function Based Gated Recurrent Unit for Mental Disorder Detection System
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Integrated Intelligence and Communication Systems (ICIICS)
abstract: The depression is a common mental health disorder that affected all around the world. The symptoms of depression such as sadness, angry, social behavior, sleep disorder and attempting suicide which are recorded from the World Health Organization (WHO). To detect the depression, sometimes classification such as depressed and not depressed are misclassified is challenged one. To overcome the problem, the research introduces the improved Self-Attention Mechanism and Balanced Loss Function based Gated Recurrent Unit (SA-BL-GRU) for mental health disorder detection system. The text and DAI- WOZ dataset contains a collection of information that provide as input to the proposed system. The collected input provided to pre-processing techniques such as data cleaning, tokenization, lemmatization and stemming to pre-process the data. The Bag of Words (BoW) is used for feature extraction phase to extract the significant features from the pre-processed data. The SA-BL-GRU is used for classification process that classify the accurate depressed and not depressed patients. The evaluation metrics such as accuracy, precision, recall and F1-score are used for estimate the performance of the evaluation metrics of 98.5%,98.3%,97.6% and 97.9% respectively.

articleTitle: Radio Attack Detection Using Deep Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Integrated Intelligence and Communication Systems (ICIICS)
abstract: The marked rise of wireless devices and the Internet of Things devices has increased the demand for wireless spectrum, leading to spectrum scarcity. Cognitive Radio Networks (CRNs) enable secondary users (SUs) to use the underutilized and unused frequency bands but are vulnerable to security threats like Byzantine and Primary User Emulation (PUE) attacks, disrupting spectrum sensing. In this work investigates use of a novel integrated spectrum sensing algorithm combining weighted sensing with Deep Q-Networks (DQN) and Generative Adversarial Networks (GAN) to optimize spectrum utilization and counteract these attacks. By using these methods can enhanced robustness against security threats, contributing advancement of CRN technologies implemented in Googlecolab and validated in MATLAB, the experimental analysis demonstrates integrated algorithm significantly outperforms basic weighted algorithm, integrated weighted algorithm got highest accuracy 99.03%.

articleTitle: Multi Robot Cooperative Control Based on Edge Computing and Multi Agent Reinforcement Learning with Cooperative Planning
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Integrated Intelligence and Communication Systems (ICIICS)
abstract: In this era, multi-robot systems play vital role in the sector of environmental monitoring, disaster response, and smart manufacturing. Previous researchers have suggested various traditional methods but still there are challenges such as high latency, bandwidth limitations, and single points of failure, making them unsuitable for time-sensitive and large-scale operations. This article is proposed to develop a system for Multi robot Cooperative Control based on edge computing by employing robust methods such as; Hierarchical Inference, dynamic workload distribution, real-time collaboration on multi-agent. Further, the hierarchical Inference is classified into three layers; cloud layer which is designed using Open Artificial Intelligence (AI) DALL-E, fog layer employed for data preprocessing using various techniques such as median filtering for noise filtering and Linear Discriminant Analysis (LDA) for dimensionality reduction and edge layer is designed by incorporating MobileViT technology. Then, the extracted features are allocated with specific task using federated learning technique namely federated averaged (FedAvg). Finally the Multi Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) with Cooperative Planning (CP) is imposed for real-time collaboration in multi agent and has resulted with 0.99 Accumulative Coverage Score (ACS) when compared to the existing Large Language Model (LLM).

articleTitle: A Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers – Multi Head Attention for Predicting the Stock Market Volatility Based on Textual Sentiment Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Integrated Intelligence and Communication Systems (ICIICS)
abstract: Recent days, stock market plays an important role in country's economic landscape, serving as a vital conduit for companies and investors to facilitate investments. As a cornerstone of economic growth. The stock market offers unparalleled opportunities for businesses to access capital and expand their operations. The existing approaches for stock market prediction based on textual sentiment analysis has gradient vanishing problems and limited parallelization. Therefore, this paper proposes Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (BERT)- Multi Head Attention which effectively enabled parallel processing and the transformer minimizes the gradient vanishing problem. Initially, the data is taken from Xueqiu investors community and the processing of text is done in three steps they are web crawling, data cleaning and data transforming. Then, this data is used for measuring volatility which helps the investors assess market risk and potential losses. Finally, proposed BERT- Multi Head Attention is used for predicting and effectively enabled the parallel processing and minimizes the problem of vanishing gradient. The proposed BERT- Multi Head Attention achieved better results in terms of accuracy of 90.65% and Fl-Score of 88.76% when compared with existing NB.

articleTitle: Enhancing Diabetic Retinopathy Detection: A Novel Ensemble Random Support Vector Gradient Model
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Integrated Intelligence and Communication Systems (ICIICS)
abstract: Globally, Diabetic Retinopathy (DR) is a major complication disease affecting millions of people, and an important cause of visual impairment for individuals with diabetics. Thus, this paper introduces a novel Ensemble Random Supportvector Gradient (ERSG) model using four important phases including data collection, pre-processing, feature extractionandclassificaation. The data collection step gathers images from three datasets namely the Diagnosis of DR, the DR-G, and the DR datasets. The next phase is to pre-process the input image, this includes three methods such as normalization, contrast enhancement, and resizing. Gray-Level Co-Occurrence Matrix (GLCM) performs the feature extraction by generating several features including contrast, correlation, energy, homogeneity, and entropy. The final phase is to detect and classify DR by applying weighted ensemble of machine learning methods such as Adaptive Support Vector, Random Forest, and eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost). A weighted Average Ensemble is employed to integrate the predictions of each classifier. Finally, comprehensive experimental analyses are conducted to affirm the detection ability of the proposed model, where several estimation keys are employed to measure its performance. The ERSG attains higher performance with higher accuracy and precision of 98.9% and 97.3% than existing DR methods.

articleTitle: A Hybrid Teaching System for Vocational College Clothing Major using Bidirectional and Auto-Regressive Transformers
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Integrated Intelligence and Communication Systems (ICIICS)
abstract: Now a days, the advent of digital technology has transformed the education sector from revolutionized traditional teaching to learning methods. This technological integrates has significantly impacted education system that leading to the development of a pedagogical approaches and enhanced student engagement. However, this technology leads to the lack of critical thinking and problem-solving skills, which is crucial for students' emotional and mental well-being. To overcome those drawbacks this paper, proposed a recommendation system based on the Deep Learning (DL). Initially, data is collected from the Tex atlas dataset, serving as the foundation for the hybrid teaching system for Vocational College Clothing. Next, a Vocational Auto Encoder is employed to extract optimal attributes from the collected data, distilling the most relevant information. Moreover, the refined data is utilized to generate new data through a robust model of Bidirectional and Auto-Regressive Transformers (BART). This proposed model leverages the extracted attributes to produce high-quality with synthetic data that can be used for various applications. Moreover, by combining these cutting-edge techniques, the process capable of producing valuable insights and augmenting existing datasets. The performance of proposed model evaluated with the various metrics and achieved accuracy of 93.67%, specificity of 94.56 %, recall of 95.26 % and precision of 93.28% by comparing with the existing Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (BERT) method on recommendation system.

articleTitle: Smart Agriculture in the Era of Big Data: IoT-Assisted Pest Forecasting and Resource Optimization for Sustainable Farming
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Integrated Intelligence and Communication Systems (ICIICS)
abstract: The goal was to facilitate quick development and revitalisation of rural areas by utilising IoT knowledge to accomplish smart agriculture against the backdrop of big data. Depleted soil fertility, increased pest attacks, and diseases are some of the climate-related risks that the agricultural sector is battling. Predicting Utilising directly sensed environmental conditions as input, a machine learning model incorporating Random Forest and the Catboost algorithm determines, based on the current environmental conditions, whether pest populations are present or not. Next, Hybrid Weighted Ant Colony Optimisation (HW ACO) is used to fine-tune the Catboost algorithm. This method evaluates the machine learning model's accuracy and precision in making predictions using test data. Predictions have been made using data from 2028 to 2022, a span of five years. Weekly forecasts are produced by the pest prediction model. With high F-measure, Precision, and Recall, the weekly predictions have an overall accuracy of 93%. Over time, the precision of the pest forecast steadily rises. Predictions for the next week are made by averaging all weather data from the past seven days. For immediate defences against pests, the weekly forecasts are crucial. The findings support sustainable farming methods and food security by showing that the device can maximise crop yields while decreasing resource consumption.

articleTitle: An Innovative Machine Learning System for Optimal Multi-Class Classification of Date Fruits by Leveraging Backward Feature Engineering to Promote Sustainable Agriculture
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Integrated Intelligence and Communication Systems (ICIICS)
abstract: Sustainable agriculture is crucial for enhancing food security and optimizing resource use, particularly in high-value crops like date fruits. Accurate multi-class classification of date fruit varieties is essential for refining agricultural practices. Traditional classification methods frequently exhibit low accuracy and susceptibility to human errors. To address these limitations, this research introduces an innovative ML framework for optimal multi-class classification of date fruit varieties. By integrating feature engineering, the framework significantly improving model accuracy and performance, demonstrating superior classification efficiency. Advanced ML models, including Optimized Trees, Ensemble, KNN, and a novel Optimized SVM, are employed to tackle the complexities of multi-class classification. The proposed Optimized SVM achieved the highest classification accuracy. These findings showcase the potential of machine learning to improve sustainable agriculture by enhancing date fruit classification accuracy. This innovative approach promotes sustainable practices, supporting smart farming and resource optimization while contributing to sustainable development through improved multi-class classification performance.

articleTitle: A Marine Traffic Pattern Prediction System Based on Graph Convolutional and Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Integrated Intelligence and Communication Systems (ICIICS)
abstract: In recent days, Marine Traffic has been an analytic provider that tracks the movement of ships and provides data like the ship's location, ship details, and weather conditions. Moreover, marine traffic supports navigators and improves the maritime traffic management system. Marine traffic can be a major cause of the collision among the ships, and it also causes the missing of the routes. To, overcome these issues this paper proposed a Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks (KAN) algorithm for prediction, effectively achieving better accuracy. Initially, data obtained from the Automatic Identification System (AIS) dataset is given as input for the preprocessing using the Pearson Correlation Coefficient (PCC) which is employed to analyze the traffic flow in the port. Later, the Density-Based Spatial Clustering of Applications with Noise (DBSAN) clustering is utilized to discover where vertex points represent a waypoint. Then Graph Convolutional Networks (GCNs) are used for the trajectory prediction to process inland waterway traffic network signals. Finally, KAN incorporates learnable activation functions that take historical weather data points as inputs, and predict resilience indices as outputs. The performance of the proposed method is evaluated with various performance metrics such as MAE, MSE, RMSE, and MAPE metrics on the AIS dataset.

articleTitle: A New Hybrid Optimization Algorithm for Reliable Clustering Routing in Wireless Sensor Network
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Integrated Intelligence and Communication Systems (ICIICS)
abstract: A wide-spread network of tiny sensor nodes is often what makes up a wireless sensor network (WSN). One or more sinks sometimes referred to as base stations (BSs), collect the data from these SNs. Compared to a standard ad-hoc network, WSNs are significantly more complex due to their intrinsic routing feature. In a wireless sensor network (WSN), nodes perform diverse tasks and are typically organized into multiple clusters according to specific requirements or metrics. This paper develops a new cluster head selection (CHS) technique for WSN using a novel hybrid algorithm called Secretary Bird Integrated Walrus Optimization (SBI-WaO). By considering QoS, throughput, network quality (reliability), energy, and risk, the best possible CHS is carried out. The final findings demonstrate the SBI-WaO algorithm's effectiveness in terms of energy, throughput, etc. With the recommended SBI-WaO approach, a high residual energy of 10.3938 is obtained.

articleTitle: High Utility Item Set Mining in Transactional Data using a Deep Learning Model
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Integrated Intelligence and Communication Systems (ICIICS)
abstract: High Utility Itemset Mining (HUIM) is an essential method in the data mining sector that helps find itemsets in transactional data that are suitable. This research proposes a original technique for HUIM by integrating Deep Learning (DL) approaches to evolution both accuracy and efficiency. We provide a DL technique that uses a neural network architecture to quantify and dynamically extract high utility itemsets (HUIs) from huge transactional datasets. In particular, the method combines Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks to record sequential dependencies within transactions with Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) for feature extraction. To additional development performance, we integrate an Ant Colony Optimization (ACO) algorithm for optimizing the DL approaches hyperparameters and the feature selection procedure. Experimental evaluation on benchmark transactional datasets, demonstrating significant improvements in mining accuracy, processing time, and overall utility discovery related to traditional HUIM approaches, providing a robust framework for data analysis and decision-making in many domains.

articleTitle: Early Detection of Sepsis by using Attention based Recurrent Neural Networks with Shapley Additive Exp lanations
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Integrated Intelligence and Communication Systems (ICIICS)

authors.preferredName: Rana Veer Samara Sihman Bharattej R

abstract: In recent years, the severe sepsis and infected shocks are becoming a maj or source of death in Intensive Care Units (ICU), which needs timely diagnosis for the effective treatment outcomes. The medical information of patients is stored in Electronic Medical records (EHR) for improvement of Artificial intelligence (AI) in medicine. However, several existing methods are utilized for sepsis detection including Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) but mostly suffer with over fitting and interpretability. To overcome these issues, Attention based Recurrent Neural Networks with Shapley Additive Explanations (ARNN-SHAP) is proposed for early detection of sepsis. The SHAP model improves the interpretability of model by higher feature importance using higher covariance of vectors. Initially, the input data is taken from MIMIC III dataset and then preprocessed with different techniques to reduce over fitting. After that, the feature importance is evaluated with the help SHAP method and fed to the ARNN classifier. The ARNN classifier classifies the data into sepsis and non-sepsis labels. From the results, the proposed ARNN-SHAP provided better results when compared to existing CNN-LSTM by providing results in terms of accuracy (90.4<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>), sensitivity (70.6%), specificity (89.7%) and precision (72.8%), Fl-score (70.4%) respectively.

articleTitle: An Automatic Extraction of Features from Water Bodies by Using Contrast Vision Transformer
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Integrated Intelligence and Communication Systems (ICIICS)
abstract: In recent days, for strengthening the climate change adaption water features are utilizing as the most crucial environmental element. The integration of Remote Sensing (RS) with Artificial Intelligence (AI) is becoming the major sought-after approach for extracting the features of water information. In existing, the Faster Regional Convolution Neural Network (FR_CNN) is utilized for the water bodies' extraction. However, the existing FR_CNN model struggled with computational complexity. To overcome this issue, Contrast Vision Transformer (CoVT) is proposed to extract features from water bodies. The transformer with self-attention mechanism reduces the computational complexity by eliminating regional proposal networks. Initially, the satellite images are taken from sentinel-2 dataset and further processed into preprocessing. In preprocessing Gaussian Median Filter (GMF) and Atmospheric Correction (AC) are utilized to reduce the noise and atmospheric effects from images. After that, proposed CoVt extract features from preprocessed images and fed into projection head to generate projected features. Finally, the projected features are further processed with prediction head to predict the satellite image features of water bodies. From the results, the proposed CoVt provided better results when compared to existing FR_CNN by providing results such as accuracy (99.4%), precision (99.1%), recall (98.5%) and F1-score (98.7%) respectively.

articleTitle: Satellite Image Scene Classification Using Roulette Fitness-Distance Balance-Based Osprey Optimization Algorithm and Bidirectional-Long Short-Term Memory Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Integrated Intelligence and Communication Systems (ICIICS)
abstract: Remote Sensing Scene Categorization (RSSC) is essential for identifying various applications, such as farms, highways, rivers, and urban areas. Accurate classification and high spatial resolution performs important role in analysis of satellite images. However, effective feature representation is essential for optimal performance, as processing sensor data can be complex. The irrelevant features causing a dimensionality challenges. This research proposes the Roulette Fitness-Distance Based Osprey Optimization Algorithm (RFDB-OOA) for feature selection to identify the most relevant features for efficient scene classification. OOA is combined with the Roulette Fitness-Distance Balance-based Method (RFDB), improve exploration ability of the algorithm and enhance a balance between exploration and exploitation. Generative Adversarial Network (GAN) utilized for augmentation process to generate augmented images, which are then processed by AlexNet and VGG19 models to extract discriminative features. Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (Bi-LSTM) network is utilized for accurate classification of images. Simulation results illustrates that the RFDB-OOA-BiLSTM approach achieves 98.67% and 99.70% on both the AID and UCM datasets as compared to the existing methods like CNN-VGG 16 and Multi-Level Semantic Feature Clustering Network (MLFC-Net).

articleTitle: Multi-Class Lung Disease Detection Using Resnet50 and Transfer Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Integrated Intelligence and Communication Systems (ICIICS)

authors.preferredName: Ravi Sri Ram G R B

abstract: Lung diseases, including Viral Pneumonia, Bacterial Pneumonia, COVID-19, Tuberculosis, and other common conditions, pose challenges in medical diagnostics. This study introduces an innovative method that merges deep learning techniques for classifying lung diseases with an AI-powered symptom checker to improve diagnostic precision and patient involvement. The proposed constructed a CNN ResNet50 architecture to categorize chest X-ray images into five distinct classes. The model underwent training and validation using an extensive dataset of labelled X-ray images, resulting in accuracy of 86% and strong performance metrics. To augment image-based diagnostic process, an incorporated generative AI model that offers users comprehensive information regarding symptoms and possible conditions based on their input. The system was implemented through user-friendly web application using Streamlit, facilitating real-time interaction and feedback. This integrated strategy aims to assist healthcare professionals in making better-informed decisions while providing patients with valuable health insights.

articleTitle: Proactive Diagnostics: Machine Learning-Driven Early Detection of Chronic Kidney Disease
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Integrated Intelligence and Communication Systems (ICIICS)
abstract: Chronic Kidney Disease (CKD) is a growing global health challenge, contributing to 10–15 % of the worldwide population's morbidity and causing 1.7 million deaths annually. Early and accurate detection is crucial for preventing severe complications like hypertension, anemia, and neurological disorders. This study presents a machine learning approach for predicting CKD using clinical data from the UCI CKD dataset, with an emphasis on four major classification algorithms: Random Forest, Decision Tree, SVM, and Naive Bayes. The study involves data preparation by handling missing values using a filtering technique, and for feature selection, a Random Forest Classifier along with Mutual Information and Pearson correlation were applied. Among the models evaluated, the Random Forest Classifier led by an accuracy of 100%, while Decision Tree, Naive Bayes, and SVM achieved accuracy of 0.975, 0.75, and 0.9916, respectively. Random Forest's handling missing data, bias reduction, and complex interactions made it effective for CKD predictions.

articleTitle: Optimizing Image Steganography: A Comparative Study of Pre-Processing Techniques and the Hybrid U-Encoder Network
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Integrated Intelligence and Communication Systems (ICIICS)
abstract: Image steganography requires balancing high fidelity, security, and imperceptibility when embedding secret information into cover images. Effective pre-processing and advanced deep learning models are essential for achieving these goals. In this study, we propose an enhanced image steganography framework that combines optimal pre-processing techniques with advanced deep learning-based models to achieve secure, high-quality image embedding. We first evaluate five distinct pre-processing methods-CLAHE, Bilateral Filtering, Gaussian Filtering, Median Filtering, and Laplacian Filtering-on cover images to determine their impact on performance metrics, including Mean Squared Error (MSE), Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE), Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio (PSNR), Structural Similarity Index (SSIM), and Normalized Cross-Correlation (NCC). Among these techniques, Bilateral Filtering demonstrated superior results with the lowest MSE (58.78), highest PSNR (30.44 dB), and near-perfect SSIM (0.948) and NCC (0.988), making it the optimal pre-processing method for steganography. Following pre-processing, two steganography models were implemented and compared: a simple concatenation-based model and a novel Hybrid U-Encoder Network inspired by U-Net architecture. The Hybrid U-Encoder Network was designed to enhance the embedding and extraction process of secret images. Comparative analysis using MSE, PSNR, and SSIM showed that the Hybrid U-Encoder Network outperformed the concatenation-based model, achieving a lower MSE of 71.55, PSNR of 58.62 dB, and SSIM of 0.982. This research highlights the importance of effective pre-processing in improving the steganography process and demonstrates the advantage of using a Hybrid U-Encoder Network for embedding secret information. By combining Bilateral Filtering with the Hybrid U-Encoder Network, the proposed approach provides a robust solution for secure and imperceptible image steganography, significantly improving the trade-off between embedding capacity and image quality.

articleTitle: Reactive Voltage Optimal Control of Distribution Networks Based on Deep Reinforcement Learning with Deep Q Network
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Integrated Intelligence and Communication Systems (ICIICS)
abstract: In recent years, reactive voltage optimal control is an advanced control methodology in modern power distribution networks. In distributed networks increased renewable energy resources became a significant challenge for unpredictable localized voltage fluctuations leads to voltage sags, swells and losses also compromise power quality and system reliability. The traditional methods which Assisted for increased renewable energy resources in distributed networks. Therefore, this paper proposes Reactive Voltage Optimal Control-Deep Q Network (RVOC-DQN) for voltage power compensation to enhance fast response time and instantaneous voltage correction. The proposed method employed on GridLAB-D dataset to integrate and control renewable energy source generation using Moving Average Filter for system faults. The preprocessed data features are extracted using Static Volt Ampere Reactive Compensators-Closed-Loop Voltage Control (SVC-CLVC) for focused control in voltage regulation to dynamic grid conditions with load and generation patterns. Finally, RVOC-DQN is employed for rapid voltage regulation and continuous operation with improved data quality in distributed networks. The proposed RVOC-DQN method attained high stability of the system in terms of Root Mean Square Error (RMSE), Correlation and values are (0.26) of RMSE and the Correlation value is (0.835) when compared with existing Active Distribution Networks.

Author Keywords: reactive voltage optimal control of distribution network

articleTitle: Prediction of Pavement Roughness using a Deep Neural Network Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Integrated Intelligence and Communication Systems (ICIICS)
abstract: One of the most important variables in pavement performance management is the International Roughness Index (IRI). Conventional IRI measurement techniques depend on costly instrumented cars and skilled personnel. The IRI updates on pavements are limited by equipment and labor expenses associated with traditional measurement models. This papers implements a unique imaging-based Deep Neural Network (DNN) model that directly determine the IRI values from pavement photos. This model demonstrated that, commonly utilized vertical accelerations or 3-dimensional (3D) images, it is possible to identify IRI using 2-dimensional (2D) images. The fast development of photographic equipment has made it little and convenient, lightweight sports action cameras, like GoPro Hero series, to combine with electronic image stabilization devices and record smooth, high-framerate videos. When compared to existing methods include Artificial Neural Network (ANN), and Radon Transform (RT), this implemented DNN method is achieved high values of 0.95 of precision in Midwest Transportation Center (MTC) dataset, and 99.6 of R ^2 of long- term pavement performance (L TTP) dataset.

articleTitle: Advanced Detection and Classification of COVID Variants Based on Omics Approach and Machine Learning Models
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Integrated Intelligence and Communication Systems (ICIICS)
abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic, driven by SARS-CoV-2, highlighted the critical need for swift and precise classification of viral variants to enhance public health measures. This research introduces a machine learning method for identifying coronavirus variants such as Alpha, Delta, and Omicron, achieving accuracy rates of up to 99%. Through feature selection methods like Mutual Information and ANOVA, along with advanced classifiers such as Gradient Boosting, Random Forest, and CatBoost, we pinpointed crucial amino acids that differentiate these variants. Our results demonstrate that machine learning improves classification accuracy, contributes to understanding the evolution of variants, and facilitates scalable viral genomics. This approach holds significant potential for advancing vaccine development and allowing for prompt, data-informed interventions.

articleTitle: Research on Enterprise Decision Support Systems Based on Artificial Intelligence Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Integrated Intelligence and Communication Systems (ICIICS)
abstract: In response to the challenge of optimizing decision support systems (DSS) for enterprises in the big data environment, this paper introduces the C4.5 decision tree algorithm and the improved Apriori algorithm, aiming to improve the classification accuracy and data correlation mining effect of the system through data mining techniques. Firstly, this paper theoretically analyzes the principles and optimization directions of C4.5 and Apriori algorithms; then, algorithm application testing is conducted on actual datasets to verify the effectiveness of the algorithm in different business scenarios, especially in the fields of retail and finance. Finally, the experimental results show that the C4.5 algorithm exhibits high accuracy and F1 score in classification task. The results show that the C4.5 decision tree algorithm effectively improves the accuracy of classification tasks, reaching 85%, with an F1 score of 85%, which is better than traditional decision tree algorithms. The model and method proposed in this paper provide new technical support and optimization directions for enterprises in big data decision support.

articleTitle: Deep Learning Architectures for Accurate Target Detection in Synthetic Aperture RADAR
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Integrated Intelligence and Communication Systems (ICIICS)
abstract: This paper presents an in-depth analysis of Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) image processing, with a focus on utilizing deep learning techniques for military vehicle identification, particularly tanks. SAR images have long been integral to the Joint Intelligence, Surveillance, and Reconnaissance (JISR) field. Building on this foundation, we propose a novel approach using deep learning architectures, namely Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN), AlexNet, and VGG16, to classify tanks into seven categories, along with a class for incorrect images. The performance of these models is thoroughly examined, with AlexN et demonstrating superior accuracy in detecting and classifying targets within SAR imagery. This study not only advances military vehicle recognition but also highlights the potential of deep learning in broader SAR-based applications, such as Automatic Target Recognition (ATR) and intelligence gathering, with implications in both military and civilian sectors.

articleTitle: Quantum Inspired Marine Predator Algorithm with Long Short-Term Memory for Detection and Classification of Chronic Kidney Disease
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Integrated Intelligence and Communication Systems (ICIICS)
abstract: Chronic Kidney Disease (CKD) is a continual decline of the kidney working time being and it is a progressive condition. The main problem with CKD is, it is asymptomatic in its early stages, this makes the early detection challenging. In order to detect the symptoms of the disease and to figure out the exact stage of the disease advance technologies have been introduced. The traditional methods failed to diagnosing the disease accurately in early stage. The paper proposed a Quantum Inspired Marine Predator Algorithm (QIMPA) in order to predict and classify the chronic kidney disease. This algorithm is employed with the marine predators using Brownian and Levy flights that uses hunting strategies. This strategy works in three phases, firstly, prey's movements and strategies are noted how it escapes from the predator, then a balanced approach is created between predator and prey. Finally, in this phase, optimization process produces a Levy flight pattern to capture the predator and prey moves at low velocity. Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) is utilized for the classification, it works by capturing the long-range values of features that enhances the diagnosing kidney disease. The proposed QIMPA model obtained 99.04% for CKD dataset compared to the existing methods.

articleTitle: Enhancing Autism Spectrum Disorder Diagnosis Using Machine Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Integrated Intelligence and Communication Systems (ICIICS)
abstract: Accurate diagnosis of autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is challenging due to its complex nature and reliance on subjective, time-consuming assessments. This study explores the use of machine learning (ML) algorithms to improve ASD diagnosis accuracy and efficiency. We evaluate multiple ML mod-els, including Random Forest, Support Vector Machine (SVM), Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP), Decision Tree, and Logistic Regression, using datasets that include genetic, behavioral, and demographic data. The aim is to identify patterns associated with ASD and assess the strengths and limitations of each model. The findings suggest that ML algorithms have the potential to revolutionize early ASD detection, offering clinicians more objective tools for timely diagnosis and intervention. Ultimately, this research contributes to advancing our understanding of ASD and supports the development of personalized treatment strategies.

articleTitle: Hand Gesture Recognition: Enhancing Accuracy and Precision with Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Integrated Intelligence and Communication Systems (ICIICS)
abstract: Accurate, real-time recognition of hand gestures in dynamic environments remains challenging in human-computer interaction. This paper presents a hybrid deep learning model combining Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) with Recurrent Neural Networks (RNN) using Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) layers to capture both spatial and temporal information for dynamic hand gesture recognition. Trained on a dataset of six gestures-scroll-left, scroll-right, scroll-up, scroll-down, zoom-in, and zoom-out-the model achieves an accuracy of 94.66%, with an F1 score of 0.94 and an AUC-ROC of 0.95, indicating significant improvement over traditional models and practical viability in real-world applications. Key topics include data preprocessing, model architecture, hardware and software configurations, and performance comparisons with benchmarks. The paper concludes with discussions on limitations and future research directions to enhance the model's adaptability and efficiency.

articleTitle: Precision Diagnosis of ADHD Subtypes with Integrated Multimodal Data
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Integrated Intelligence and Communication Systems (ICIICS)
abstract: Attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) is one of the most prevalent neurodevelopmental disorders impacting children and adolescents. In neurodevelopmental research, ADHD subtypes provide a major issue since there are not enough reliable biomarkers to classify them. This study investigates the predictive potential of ADHD subtypes using a multimodal dataset, including behavioural measures, self-reported symptoms, and EEG data. The study utilized Principal Component Analysis (PCA) to reduce dimensionality, while Random Forest (RF) classifiers were employed for predicting subtypes. The research work achieved a cross-validation accuracy of 96.6% and test accuracy of 95.2%, outperforming both KNN and SVM. Feature importance analysis highlighted that self-reported symptoms were the most significant predictors of DSM subtypes, with neuropsychological data outperforming EEG features for subtype classification. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of several measurement modalities in categorizing ADHD subtypes and emphasize the necessity of accurate assessment methods to improve diagnostic precision and guide focused intervention practices.

articleTitle: ImmunoYield: A Smart Greenhouse for Disease Detection and Prevention
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Integrated Intelligence and Communication Systems (ICIICS)
abstract: Traditional farming methods rely heavily on manual labor and are subject to unpredictable yields due to various environmental and biological factors. To address these challenges, proposing “ImmunoYield,” an automated greenhouse system that integrates sensor technology and deep learning for optimizing farm conditions and early disease detection in crops. The system employs humidity, light, and soil sensors for real-time monitoring and control, while a Convolutional Neural Network model is utilized for diagnosing plant diseases through image analysis. Results from experiments indicate that this system reduces the water usage by approximately 30% and increases crop yield by 15% compared to traditional farming methods. Additionally, our deep learning model demonstrates an 86% accuracy in plant disease detection, improving to 80% in real-time testing with new inputs. The suggested approach not only lowers manual labor but also enhances productivity and cost-efficiency, making it a promising solution for modern agriculture. Future work will focus on enhancing the system's generalization capabilities and exploring integration with additional sustainable technologies.

articleTitle: An Intelligent Context Based Movie Recommendation System Using Bi-Directional Gated Recurrent Unit
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Integrated Intelligence and Communication Systems (ICIICS)
abstract: In recent years, there is the rapid expansion of digital content and streaming platforms. There are several existing recommendation systems developed based on collaborative filtering and content-based filtering but still they face challenges such as privacy concerns, overcoming the cold-start problem for new users, managing scalability for large datasets, and mitigating biases in recommendations. The motive of this study is to develop a robust movie recommendation system that enhances user satisfaction by offering content tailored to individual perceptions. This paper suggests a novel approach to develop an effective movie recommendation model using Bi-Directional Gated Recurrent Unit (Bi-GRU). The proposed Bi-GRU recommendation model is imposed on a Movie Lens dataset for movie preferences. Firstly, at the classification stage, Auto Regressive Integrated Moving Average and Convolutional Neural Networks (ARIMA-CNN) is employed to classify the movies with the assistance of temporal data. Furthermore, Bi-Directional Gated Recurrent Unit (Bi-GRU) is employed is incorporated for recommendation model as it can assist in summarization of the text and enhancement of the model this review from the audience signifies optimistic movie recommendation. The Bi-GRU model outperformed the existing method i.e. Unsupervised Boltzmann Machine-Based Time-Aware Recommendation System (UBMTR) by providing effective results in RSME (0.62), MAPE (0.38).

articleTitle: Advanced Machine Learning Approaches for Infant Cry Classification using Audio Feature Extraction
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Integrated Intelligence and Communication Systems (ICIICS)
abstract: This study develops a machine learning framework to classify infant cries using 457 audio features, including time domain features like Zero-Crossing Rate (ZCR) for frequency analysis and Quadratic Mean RMS for power measurement. Frequency-domain features, notably Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCCs), alongside Mel-spectrograms and Time Series Imaging (TSI) provide detailed visualization of audio signals. The data is split into 80% training and 20% testing sets with 10-fold cross-validation for tuning. Several machine learning models, including Logistic Regression, Support Vector Classifier, Decision Trees, Random Forests, and XGBoost, are evaluated. Hyperparameter tuning through grid search shows the Random Forest model with MFCC features achieves a peak accuracy of 98.03%. Evaluation using accuracy, confusion matrices, and feature importance highlights MFCC's role in classification. Results demonstrate the effectiveness of combining machine learning with classical feature extraction for infant cry classification, supporting early health monitoring. Future work includes ensemble techniques to boost performance.

articleTitle: Enhanced Multi-Layer Bat Optimization(EMBO) Approach for Data Acquisition and Security Management in Web Platform
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Integrated Intelligence and Communication Systems (ICIICS)
abstract: Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS) have grown to be essential to network and computer security. However, it complicates the training phase and makes it time-consuming to detect vulnerabilities in data sharing on the network. To solve this problem, we introduced a Multi-Layer Perceptron Neural Network (MLPNN) technique in data science to classify malicious and non-malicious network traffic. In addition, we preprocess the data by normalizing the mean original value using the Z-score Min-Max Scaling (ZSMMS) technique. In addition, we select the best feature by analyzing the weight and bias values with the Improved Bat Optimization (IBO) algorithm. After that, we propose the MLPNN technique to classify network traffic and improve accuracy. Finally, the Optimal Padding Advanced Encryption Standard (OPAES) algorithm will be implemented to enhance the security of the website. Additionally, by producing an IDS model and using metrics such as accuracy, recall, time complexity, and security performance, the website's security performance can be improved to 95.7%.

articleTitle: Enhanced Hill Cipher Algorithm with Novel Encoding and Key Generation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Integrated Intelligence and Communication Systems (ICIICS)
abstract: This research article presents a modified Hill Cipher algorithm that incorporates a novel alphanumeric encoding scheme, for the extended character set that includes alphabets, digits, and space characters. It employs a novel non-sequential encoding scheme aims to provide enhanced security by avoiding predictable character mapping. It also uses a novel approach to key generation, employing a random selection of numbers within a specific range of digits, which significantly accelerates the key generation process faster than the traditional Hill Cipher algorithm. With a character set of 37 (alphabets (26), digits (10) and space), the prime modulus 37 is used in the Hill Cipher, which eliminates the need for the GCD check, that helps in lowering the computational complexity. Further, it has been found that the proposed Hill Cipher provides enhanced efficiency, security, and versatility by generating varied cipher texts for the same character and same cipher text for different plaintext characters.

articleTitle: Education System based on Pre- Training with Extracted Gap-Sentences for Abstractive Summarization Sequence-to-Sequence and Bidirectional Auto-Regressive Transformers
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Integrated Intelligence and Communication Systems (ICIICS)
abstract: In present scenario, the traditional education system has criticized for its one-size-fits-all approach, failing to provide to individual students' needs. The advent of technology has brought about opportunities to revolutionize education that aims to investigate the feasibility of developing an education system by addressing the existing challenges that overreliance on technology, inadequate teacher training, unequal access to digital resources existing inequalities and academic challenges. To overcome those drawbacks, this paper proposed a robust educational system by harnessing effective methods. Initially, preprocessing techniques like tokenization, stop word removal, stemming, and lemmatization are applied to the data. The processed data is then fed into the Extended Technology Acceptance Model (ETAM), which extracts optimal attributes like academic performance and grades. Leveraging these extracted parameters to an education system for developing advanced text generation models, Pre-Training with Extracted Gap-Sentences for Abstractive Summarization Sequence- To-Sequence (PEGASUS) and Bidirectional and Auto-Regressive Transformers (BART). This proposed model enables the generation of high-quality educational content, facilitating personalized learning experiences by combining these cutting-edge techniques. The performance of proposed model Pegasus-BART evaluated with the various metrics such accuracy with value of (96.56%), Precision is (94.63%), Recall is (96.04%), and F1 score is (95.77%) respectively.

Author Keywords: pre-training with extracted gap-sentences for abstractive summarization sequence-to-sequence

articleTitle: Assessing Machine Learning Models for Predictive Analytics in Urban Rental Markets: Rent Price Forecasting in India
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Integrated Intelligence and Communication Systems (ICIICS)
abstract: This research marks a groundbreaking application of a diverse array of machine learning techniques to predict rental house prices specifically in the major Indian cities of Pune, Delhi, and Mumbai. These urban areas are known for their rapid economic growth and complex demographic shifts, which introduce significant variability into the rental market. Moving beyond the conventional focus on property sales, this study explores the rental market using advanced machine learning models such as Linear Regression, Ridge, Lasso, ElasticNet, Random Forest, Gradient Boosting, K-Neighbors, Decision Tree, Support Vector Machines, and Polynomial Regression. This novel approach is tailored to meet the unique challenges of the Indian rental landscape, offering a detailed examination that transcends traditional analytic methods. By meticulously adapting these models to the nuanced dynamics of rental prices in Pune, Delhi, and Mumbai, the study fills a crucial gap in existing real estate research. Our results highlight the varied performance of these models, with non-linear methods like K-Neighbors and Random Forest emerging as particularly effective in capturing the complex interplays affecting rental prices. This research not only deepens the understanding of machine learning's utility in real estate analytics but also provides vital data-driven insights to stakeholders involved in policymaking, investing, and managing within India's vibrant and evolving rental markets.

Index Terms: Least Absolute Shrinkage And Selection Operator

articleTitle: Data Collection and Preprocessing Management for Sugarcane Leaf Disease Identification Using by Spatial Relation-Assisted Contrast Enhancement (SRCE)
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Integrated Intelligence and Communication Systems (ICIICS)
abstract: Background: Sugarcane, an essential commodity for the global sugar industry, is very vulnerable to several illnesses that significantly impact its output and quality. Methods: The study uses Spatial Relation Assisted Contrast Enhancement (SRCE) to enhance contrast in images of harmed sugarcane leaves. SRCE selectively enhances contrast, allowing for better differentiation between healthy and diseased areas. It focuses on local neighborhoods, highlighting critical symptoms while preserving leaf structure and texture. The enhanced images were analyzed using machine learning classifiers to assess their effectiveness in disease detection. Result: The results demonstrated that SRCE significantly improved the detection accuracy compared to traditional contrast enhancement techniques. This method aids in early disease identification and supports precision agriculture practices by enabling timely interventions. The results of SRCE of CII, LIF, SSIM, and PSNR values are evaluated. Conclusion: Our findings suggest that SRCE can be a valuable agricultural monitoring and management tool, ultimately contributing to increased sugarcane yield and sustainability.

articleTitle: Deep Learning Based Covid-19 Diagnosis and Severity Assessment Using Computed Tomography Imaging
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Integrated Intelligence and Communication Systems (ICIICS)
abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic has highlighted the need for advanced diagnostic tools for early detection and management. This study presents a Deep Learning (DL) approach using CT scans to detect COVID-19 and assess lung involvement. A Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) achieves 94% accuracy in distinguishing COVID-positive from negative cases. Image preprocessing, including Gaussian blurring and Otsu's thresholding, enhances lung region clarity. Lung segmentation isolates critical areas, enabling severity classification (mild, moderate, severe) based on opacity-to-lung area ratio. Using the SARS-CoV-2 CT dataset, the CNN model with Transfer Learning (TL) via ResNet reaches 96.74 % accuracy. This method provides a valuable diagnostic tool for real-time healthcare decision-making during pandemics.

articleTitle: Detection of Vocal Nodules from Phonation Data Using Spectral Features and Recurrence Plots
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Integrated Intelligence and Communication Systems (ICIICS)
abstract: Vocal nodules are one of the most common forms of voice pathology which, if neglected, can grow and even become cancerous. Diagnosis of vocal nodules involves video stroboscopy in hospital conditions, and is often missed in the early stages which are treatable without surgery. Hence, simple methods based on phonation have gained prominence in diagnosis of voice pathologies. In this work, a novel feature extraction method based on a combination of MFCC and nonlinear recurrence plots is proposed. To compare the performance of this method, comparative results on a standard public dataset, and on the first clinically acquired dataset on an Indian population are presented. The proposed method yields a best accuracy of over 95% on the SVD as well as on the hospital-acquired dataset. The algorithm correctly classifies several early nodule data present in SRIHER data. It is shown that the misclassification occurs due to a few specific samples in the dataset. This work shows that recurrence plots can be a valuable additional feature for population-agnostic accurate detection of vocal nodules.

articleTitle: A Paper of RF Low Noise Amplifier Using Ku Band
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Integrated Intelligence and Communication Systems (ICIICS)
abstract: LNA is short for low noise amplifier and it is a fundamental active component in RF chain reception. It has to meet a line of specifications including power gain, noise figure, insertion loss, and even power consumption. A two-stage LNA working in the band 12–18 GHz employs active biased circuitry as well as inductive source degeneration topology to achieve high gain and low noise. Such stability analysis is performed in the software environment of ADS employing stability coefficients while the input and output impedance are tuned using a Smith chart as reference. For the entire system operating in this frequency band, journals report design approaches that are mostly hybrid or MMIC in nature. Inductors and capacitors are chosen to gain and noise figure performance targets. The workshop is configured and programmed in ADS for practical use in the field.

articleTitle: Analysis of Single Grain Structure and Quality Monitoring of Rice Under High Temperature Stress
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Integrated Intelligence and Communication Systems (ICIICS)
abstract: High temperature stress affects the physiological and biochemical indicators of rice, and directly affects the quality of rice. This article uses field experiments and laboratory analysis methods to systematically study the structure and quality of single rice grains under high temperature stress. After harvesting, the appearance and internal structure of individual seeds were carefully observed and analyzed using optical microscopy and scanning electron microscopy. Meanwhile, by combining quality indicators such as grain weight, grain moisture content, starch content, and protein content, the comprehensive impact of high temperature stress on rice grain quality is evaluated. The experimental results show that increasing irrigation has a positive effect on all varieties, especially on the yield and survival rate of varieties A and B. This indicates that appropriate water supplementation is crucial for helping plants resist high temperature stress. This study revealed the mechanism of the impact of high temperature stress on the structure and quality of rice single grains through systematic field experiments and indoor analysis.

articleTitle: Improved Industrial Internet Edge Computing Task Unloading Strategy
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Integrated Intelligence and Communication Systems (ICIICS)
abstract: With the rapid development of the industrial Internet, the number of industrial devices has increased dramatically, generating a huge amount of data, which puts forward higher requirements for real-time processing. The traditional cloud computing model faces latency and bandwidth bottlenecks in processing real-time data in industrial Internet, and edge computing emerges. This paper focuses on the edge computing task offloading strategy in the industrial Internet environment to solve the problems caused by the uneven distribution of computing resources and the complexity of task offloading decision. In this paper, for the problem of edge computing task offloading in the industrial Internet environment, a link performance-aware task offloading transmission path algorithm is proposed, and the ITGO algorithm is improved. Experimental results show that the algorithm can effectively reduce the task transmission delay and improve the overall throughput and stability of the system under high load environment.

articleTitle: Enhanced Security in Cloud Storage Systems Based on Adaptive Thresholding with Dual Attention Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Integrated Intelligence and Communication Systems (ICIICS)
abstract: Recent days, cloud storage has revolutionized data management system by providing a flexible, on demand outsourcing solution that eliminated storage management complexities, reduced capital expenditures on hardware and software, which minimized maintenance requirements. Traditional approaches for enhanced security in cloud storage systems had faced significant challenges, which include increased complexity and compatibility issues. Therefore, this paper proposes Adaptive Thresholding-Dual Attention Neural Networks (AT-DANN) which is employed on Benchmarking Evaluation Toolkit for Hypervisor (BETH) dataset. This dataset is preprocessed by using secure Deduplication system, which optimize storage efficiency. Then, content-based chunking and fingerprinting which effectively breaks the data into smaller chunks. After that, proposed AT-DANN is used to adjust threshold values based on data distribution and variability and focused on relevant data features and contexts. This context are hashed by using Multiple Hashing to ensure data consistency and finally, Cross domain authentication is utilized for enabling secure data sharing between different organizations. the proposed AT-DNN for enhanced security in cloud storage systems achieved better results accuracy ratio (89 %), performance ratio (75%), encryption ratio (80 %), efficiency ratio (90 %), evaluation ratio (75 %) when compared with existing Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN).

articleTitle: Adult Obesity Prediction with Ensemble Classification Techniques - A Deep Learning Strategy
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Integrated Intelligence and Communication Systems (ICIICS)
abstract: The development of precise prediction models for early intervention is of the utmost importance due to the significant public health issue of the increasing prevalence of adult obesity. The study introduces an innovative approach for adult obesity prediction using deep learning and ensemble classification techniques. The current proposed approach is trying to overcome previous approaches in terms of robustness and accuracy. Normally, the proposed method is improving the prediction in performance by collecting various classifiers into one framework based on deep learning. Several classifiers are considered here, such as decision trees, SVMs, k-nearest neighbors. The system employs dynamic weighting modification scheme that optimizes input from every classifier within the training phase. On such a large dataset, experiments indicate that the proposed model is much more reliable and accurate compared to standard single-model methods for adult obesity prediction. These results showed that public health professionals may benefit from the ensemble learning that improves obesity prediction with a potential accuracy of 86.7<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup> in monitoring populations and responding promptly, when necessary.

articleTitle: Breast Cancer Image Classification Using Convolutional Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Integrated Intelligence and Communication Systems (ICIICS)
abstract: This study aimed to develop and evaluate a deep learning-based classification model for breast ultrasound images. The primary objectives were to classify ultrasound images into three categories: benign, malignant, and normal. Breast cancer detection using ultrasound imaging is challenging due to class imbalance and insufficient annotations in datasets. This research focuses on enhancing classification accuracy by leveraging a pre-trained ResNet-50 model. Methods included data augmentation to address class imbalance and the integration of masks overlayed on ultrasound images to emphasize regions of interest. These enhancements significantly improved the model's ability to distinguish between benign, malignant, and normal breast tissue. The model achieved an accuracy of 98%, up from an initial 86% on unseen data, demonstrating the impact of detailed annotations and fine-tuning. The results underscore the potential of AI-driven models in improving diagnostic accuracy. Future work involves incorporating additional data sources and validating the model across diverse clinical settings, with the goal of advancing early detection and personalized treatment strategies in breast cancer care.

articleTitle: Identifying Earthquake Damages in Building Using Random Forest Classifier Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Integrated Intelligence and Communication Systems (ICIICS)
abstract: Detecting damaged buildings quickly after an earthquake is crucial for emergency teams to save lives. Existing methods for earthquake damage prediction in buildings face challenges related to accuracy and efficiency, particularly in quickly identifying damaged structures post-disaster. These challenges are overcome by the proposed approach using simple machine learning models to predict the stiff ness, strength, and displacement ratios of damaged materials based on observed crack features and loading conditions. This paper proposes an approach that combines classification by Decision Tree (DT) and regression tasks to calculate the damages using an earthquake prediction dataset. The numerical validation of the proposed method results in an accuracy of 0.893, a recall of 0.891, and an F1-score of 0.813, indicating its effectiveness. Compared to existing methods such as Artificial Neural Network (ANN), Support Vector Machine (SVM), VGG-16, and K-nearest neighbor (KNN), the proposed method overcomes limitations and enhances performance in identifying damaged structures.

articleTitle: Early Diagnosis of Lung Cancer Using Hyperparameter-Tuned Machine Learning Models
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Integrated Intelligence and Communication Systems (ICIICS)
abstract: Globally, lung cancer is the leading cause of cancer-related deaths. Improving survival depends on early and precise identification, which is still mostly accomplished using antiquated techniques that are frequently ineffective and erroneous. In this study, we used patient demographic and clinical data to create a machine learning-based risk prediction model that aims to diagnose lung cancer early and accurately. To verify the performance on our lung cancer data set, we employed important machine learning algorithms such as logistic regression, random forest, and support vector machines (SVM). PCA for feature selection, resampling to balance classes, and handling missing values were all examples of preprocessing. Among models, Random Forest shown excellent efficiency in risk detection, while SVM ultimately.

articleTitle: Research on a Prototype System of Spatial Big Data Approximation Query for Smart City Based on Cloud Computing
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Integrated Intelligence and Communication Systems (ICIICS)
abstract: Smart city spatial query is a data structure that arranges spatial objects in a certain order based on their location and shape, or a certain spatial relationship between spatial objects. It aims to quickly filter spatial objects that are unrelated to specific spatial operations and is an important indicator for ensuring efficient search and display of spatial data. Its performance directly affects the overall performance of geographic information systems and spatial databases. At present, various spatial approximation query algorithms have been optimized, but there are still significant limitations. This article empirically tests the relationship between smart cities and high-quality development of the circulation industry based on the spatial DID model. The trajectory data is divided into sub trajectories using a trajectory data partitioning method based on optimized minimum boundary rectangle MBR to improve the approximation effect of trajectory data. The results show that the optimal convergence speed of our method is 50 times, and the convergence accuracy is the highest, with a maximum value of 1.5160, a minimum value of 1.6623, and an average value of 1.54471. When the data volume is 3.0, the running time of the method in this article is 560ms. Based on cloud computing systems, the efficiency and accuracy of window queries and spatial connection queries are the highest, and the algorithm has high adaptability.

articleTitle: Securing IoT Data Transmission with Deep Learning Approach to Steganography with Convolutional Neural Networks and Generative Adversarial Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Integrated Intelligence and Communication Systems (ICIICS)
abstract: In the evolving Internet of Things (IoT) landscape, network data security is a critical concern due to vulnerabilities like weak passwords, insecure networks, and outdated components. This project tackles these challenges by introducing an innovative encryption method that conceals IoT network data within image files. By addressing key vulnerabilities, this approach enhances data transmission security. The project employs Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) and Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs), integrated into traditional steganography techniques to increase payload capacity and se-cure data transfer. Testing results demonstrate a 0.4000 increase in accuracy (achieving 90.04%), a significant reduction in loss by 0.4525, and improved image quality with a Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio (PSNR) increase of 23.8752, showcasing the model's robustness in real-time encoding and decoding. The ultimate objective is to provide a comprehensive solution to strengthen IoT data security in the face of emerging threats.

articleTitle: Structural Health Monitoring and Damage Detection Using Namib-Beetle Optimization Algorithm with 1D Convolutional Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Integrated Intelligence and Communication Systems (ICIICS)
abstract: Structural Health Monitoring and damage detection in structures, buildings and roadways are an eminently vital field due to the widespread utility of the method, ranging from public security to civil application. Numerous architectures are used for extraction, selection and classification to detect the location, extent of the damage and monitor the structure. However, traditional dimensionality reduction methods exhibit poor-accuracy in dealing with non-linear distributions which manifest at higher Degrees of Freedom in vehicle-bridge interactions. This work proposes a Namib-Beetle Optimization Algorithm (NBOA) with 1D-Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) which helps to minimize the feature cost function and effectively capture sequential time series data in classification in structural health monitoring and damage detection. In the preprocessing step, frequency transformation, signal averaging and normalization procedures are considered to eliminate the stochastic nature of time domain processes and then, an Adversarial Auto-Encoder (AAE) architecture is used to perform feature extraction and understand the latent space in the architecture. NBOA is used to perform feature selection and 1D-CNN performs classification with reduced computation and an increased attention to features. The proposed NBOA with 1D-CNN achieves an Area Under the Curve (AUC) value of 0.987 compared to the existing methods like Convolutional Auto- Encoder module and U-Net based Auto-Encoder module.

articleTitle: Securing loT Systems with AI-Infused Software and Virtual Replica Models
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Integrated Intelligence and Communication Systems (ICIICS)
abstract: The proliferation of Internet of Things (loT) devices has introduced significant security challenges due to the increased attack surface and the inherent vulnerabilities of interconnected systems. This paper proposes a novel security framework that integrates Artificial Intelligence (AI)-infused software and Virtual Replica Models, or Digital Twins, to enhance the robustness of loT systems. The framework leverages AI-driven anomaly detection and predictive analysis to identify potential threats in real-time, while Digital Twins provide a virtual replica of the loT ecosystem for continuous monitoring and simulation-based threat assessment. By fusing these technologies, the proposed solution enables proactive security measures, ensuring rapid response to cyberattacks and continuous system optimization. Extensive simulations and experimental results demonstrate the system's ability to reduce attack detection times by 30%, while improving overall system resilience and minimizing false positive rates.
