abstract: This paper presents a novel Charge Trap Cell (CTC) inverter implementation for a 10-transistor Static Random Access Memory (SRAM) architecture, aimed at accelerating the training process of Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) by optimizing Multiply and Accumulate (MAC) operations. By performing MAC operations directly within the memory using charge trapping mechanisms, the design enables efficient local data retention, reducing reliance on external data transfers between secondary memory and processor. This approach not only enhances data processing speed but also improves overall computational efficiency, leading to faster CNN training cycles. Although the complete Charge Trap Cell SRAM (CTC-SRAM) architecture is still conceptual, the successful implementation of the CTC inverter provides a strong foundation as it provides 90% similarity to conventional MOSFET inverters, confirming its reliability for scaling it to SRAM.

articleTitle: An Intelligent Personalized Music Recommendation System Using Content-Based Filtering with Convolutional Recurrent Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Integrated Intelligence and Communication Systems (ICIICS)
abstract: N owadays, the emotion of every individual human is detected according to the user's facial expressions. The rapid growth of technologies in music information retrieval, personalized music recommendation systems remain in the beginning stage only. However, the personalized music suggestions are common, but, recommending songs based on emotions remains a significant challenge. Hence, this research proposes a Deep Learning (DL) based Convolutional Recurrent Neural Network with Content-Based Filtering (CRNN-CBF) model to recommend personalized music based on emotion. At first, the data gathered from Facial Emotion Recognition 2013 (FER2013) dataset and the collected images are preprocessed by median filter, histogram equalization, and a wiener filter. Then, features are extracted by using Linear Binary Patterns (LBP) method and then classified using CRNN, categorizing images into seven distinct types of user emotions. Next, spotify Application Programming Interface (API) is employed to deliver playlists and finally, CBF is introduced to recommend personalized music according to user interests. From the results, the proposed CRNN-CBF model achieved outstanding results in accuracy 95.73%, precision 94.86%, and recall 96.78% when compared with existing model such as Emotion-Aware Music Recommendation System by using Deep Neural Network (EA-DNN).

articleTitle: Golden Sine Strategy-Fire Hawk Optimization for Energy-Efficient Resource Allocation in IoT-Based Cloud-Fog Environments
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Integrated Intelligence and Communication Systems (ICIICS)
abstract: The rapid growth of Internet of Things (IoT) has created significant demand for effective resource management in cloud-fog platforms. Therefore, there is a need for efficient resource allocation in the IoT environment to avoid unnecessary delays. In this paper, a novel method named Golden Sine Strategy-Fire Hawk Optimization (GSS-FHO) is proposed for resource allocation in IoT-based cloud-fog systems. GSS-FHO minimizes latency, improves resource usage, and decreases energy consumption by optimally allocating resources to end users. It also overcomes challenges of existing metaheuristic optimization algorithms by integrating golden ratio and sine functions, while also enabling balanced exploration-exploitation, thus improving the overall performance and solving the local optimum issues. Additionally, the performance of GSS-FHO is compared with that of the conventional algorithms like Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Whale Optimization Algorithm (WOA) for analysis. The experimental results showcase the effectiveness of GSS-FHO as a reliable solution for dynamic cloud-fog platforms. When compared to existing methods, GSS-FHO reduces the load to 0.003, energy consumption to 0.12, and migration cost to 0.002, thereby demonstrating the proposed method's effective strategy for resource allocation.

articleTitle: Leveraging SVM for Accurate Multiple Disease Prediction in Healthcare
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Integrated Intelligence and Communication Systems (ICIICS)
abstract: Accurate disease prediction plays a vital role in healthcare, with recent advancements in machine learning (ML) and artificial intelligence (AI) driving this field forward. This paper presents a multi-disease prediction system that leverages advanced ML algorithms - Random Forest, Support Vector Machine (SVM), and Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) to predict diseases like diabetes, Parkinson's, and heart disease. By analyzing complex medical datasets, the system detects critical trends and risk factors. With an intuitive interface powered by Streamlit Cloud, users can select a specific disease, enter relevant health information, and receive customized predictions. This innovative tool improves early detection accuracy, providing proactive health management support for both individuals and healthcare providers. This system aids in precise and forecasts the patients profile and disease.

articleTitle: Green Roof Optimization Using Multi Objective Optimization with Genetic Programming Based Artificial Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Integrated Intelligence and Communication Systems (ICIICS)
abstract: In recent years, the greenhouse gases are rising increasingly and the extreme usage of vestige energy resources helped in the green spaces development including green roof systems, which is an important focus in urban areas. In existing, green roof designs are optimized with different methods such as Fuzzy framework-based optimization. However, the framework is a single object based optimization so, the framework struggle to handle multi conflict objects. To overcome this issue, Multi Objective Optimization with Genetic Programming based Artificial Neural Network (MOO-GPANN) is proposed to optimize the green roof design. Initially, the input data is taken from NYC Green Roof Footprints (NYC-GRF) dataset and further processed into feature extraction with fuzzy if-then rule. Then, the optimal features are selected by using Multi Objective Optimization (MOO) based on ranking diversity. Finally, the prediction done by using Genetic Programming based Artificial Neural Network (GPANN). From the results, the proposed MOO-GPANN model gave better results than existing Adaptive Neuro-Fuzzy Inference System (ANFIS) by providing results for the objective functions including energy consumption (PMV), Heating Load (HL), Cooling Load (CL) and comfort levels (CFL) respectively.

articleTitle: DbISCDP: An Empirical Study on Distance-Based Nearest Neighbor Approaches for Credit Default Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Integrated Intelligence and Communication Systems (ICIICS)
abstract: Financial institutions usually use expert systems based on artificial intelligence to make credit lending a successful venture. However, the problem is made worse because these systems are typically not tailored to the lender's requirements and the instances are frequently quite diverse. Because of this, understanding the existing data is crucial for better insight. Since distance measures play a pivotal role in machine learning analytics, the focus has been given to the distance metrics utilized in the k-Nearest Neighbour (k-NN) algorithm. As the underlying structure of the data used to differ for datasets, focus has been given primarily to credit risk datasets. As no prior studies have been done on finding optimal distance metrics for credit risk datasets, the objective of the study is to find it. An appropriate distance metric for credit risk datasets can accurately determine the closest neighboring points which will help in decision making. For this, seven distance metric families with thirteen different distance measures have been considered in this scope. To get better insight, an expert system was proposed named Distance-based Intelligent System for Credit Default Prediction or DbISCDP utilizing lO-fold cross-validation for training and testing. In terms of average accuracy, Cosine and Hassanat distances provide better results for German and Australian benchmark datasets, respectively.

articleTitle: Concatenated Residual Attention U-Net with DenseNet: A Hybrid Deep Learning Framework for Pavement Condition Evaluation and Maintenance Planning
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Integrated Intelligence and Communication Systems (ICIICS)
abstract: Recent days, pavement management systems are important for country's economic well-being as road authorities strive to protect their valuable road assets and minimize the maintenance costs which optimize resource allocation. Traditional approaches for accurate pavement condition evaluation faced significant challenges which include infrequent evaluations lead to delayed maintenance by causing further deterioration, insufficient funding lead to inadequate maintenance. Therefore, this paper proposes a Deep Learning (DL) based Concatenated Residual Attention U-Net with DenseNet (CRAUNet-DenseNet) for Accurate Pavement Condition Evaluation and Maintenance Planning. Initially, data is collected from pavement surface images by using two images. Then, preprocessing is done by using data augmentation to improve training process. After that, image segmentation is done by CRAUNet where, it has encoder, decoder, and skip connection parts to make image segments as well as restore feature maps to its original size. The image features were extracted by utilizing Spatial Pyramid Pooling Layer (SPPL) which allows arbitrary scales of any sizes of image. At last, DenseN et is used for determining and classify condition of road from pavement surface images. The proposed CRAUNet-DenseN et model generated outperforming results in precision 97.91 %, recall 98.36%, and F1 score 99.10% when compared with existing Convolutional Neural Network (CNN).

articleTitle: Nanotechnology-Enhanced Multipliers: Leveraging FinFET and GnrFET in Advanced Digital Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Integrated Intelligence and Communication Systems (ICIICS)
abstract: Multipliers find applications in high-performance computing and advanced digital systems, where speed and energy efficiency are crucial. Existing Fin Field Effect Transistor (FET) multipliers face challenges such as high-power consumption and significant propagation delays due to limitations in scaling and increased short-channel effects. These issues hinder performance and efficiency significantly as technology nodes shrink. The proposed Dynamic Path Auto-Configurable Multipliers (DPAM) leverages FET (FinFET) and graphene nanoribbon FET (GnrFET) technologies to enhance speed and reduce power consumption. By incorporating Reconfigurable Booth Encoding (RBE), the multiplier efficiently handles large data values with reduced complexity and increased speed. The Dynamic Path Auto-configuration Adder (DPAA) optimizes the carry propagation paths, improving performance and energy efficiency. Integrating these advanced technologies results in a multiplier with superior characteristics compared to conventional designs. The performance metrics of DPAM include Total Path Delay (TPD) at 44.681 ns, Carry Out Rise Delay (CORD) at 43.180 ps, and Carry Out Fall Delay (COFD) at 40.902 ps, indicating efficient signal propagation. The Sum Rise Delay (SRD) is recorded at 43.190 ns, and the Sum Fall Delay (SFD) is 44.756 ns, showcasing balanced and stable operational delays. These values reflect the system's optimized delay characteristics for high-speed computational tasks.

articleTitle: Cloud based Automatically Human Document Authentication Processes for Secured System
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Integrated Intelligence and Communication Systems (ICIICS)
abstract: Ensuring that document authentication is safe and secure is a significant problem in contemporary cloud systems. To resolve this problem, a cloud-based automatic document authentication process in secured systems using the Risk Based Authentication (RBA) approach has been developed. The proposed system passes through three primary phases to maintain credible levels of security. First, the PKG method produces private keys for a user to achieve the goals of privacy and integrity. Second, the RBA method supports the authentication process, applying appropriate authentication management that depends on the user's risk profile and behavioral pattern. Finally, to protect data during transmission from external interference, the RSA encryption-decryption method ensures that data arrives in its original form without interference. This multiple approach to enhancing security performance is far better than the previous methods. The proposed system resource that hosts the system achieves a security performance of 95.7%

articleTitle: The Role of Chatbots and Virtual Assistants in Enhancing Customer Service and Engagement: A Stacked BiLSTM and A-GRU Technique
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Integrated Intelligence and Communication Systems (ICIICS)
abstract: By analyzing the performance of machine learning-powered chatbots and virtual assistants, this approach seeks to automate customer support. To keep up with the ever-increasing need for scalable, efficient, and quick customer service, businesses are increasingly relying on DL and other innovative technologies. These technologies are being utilized to enhance customer support operations, and this proposal compares their effectiveness to that of more traditional types of assistance. Preprocessing, feature selection, and model training are all part of the suggested method. The purpose of preprocessing is to convert it into identically lengthened sequences of numbers. Problems with intuition and specification make up feature selection. During the whole training process, the Stacked A-GRU-BiLSTM model was continually employed. Compared to GRU and BiLSTM, this cutting-edge approach achieves a mean accuracy of 93.29%.

articleTitle: An Effective Stroke Prediction Based on Cat Boost with Few Short Compound Activity
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Integrated Intelligence and Communication Systems (ICIICS)

authors.preferredName: Rana Veer Samara Sihman Brahmatej Rupavath

abstract: In recent years, strokes are becoming a maj or global health concern that affecting the welfare of the population. Many researches have focused on developing predictive models using Machine Learning (ML) and Deep Learning (DL) for strokes. However, the existing method Support Vector Machine (SVM) used to predict the strokes but struggled with sensitivity issues. To overcome this issue, Cat Boost with Few-Shot Compound Activity Prediction (CB-FSCAP) is proposed for stroke prediction. The Few-Shot Compound Activity Prediction (FSCAP) effectively learns the representation from labeled data to reduce the sensitivity issues. Primarily, the input data is taken from healthcare-dataset-stroke-data dataset and the further processed into preprocessing. The stop words are removed and imputation, lemmatization are utilized to reduce dimensionality in preprocessing. Then, the preprocessed data is fed into Cat Boost (CB) for selecting the optimal features. Finally, prediction is done with the help of FSCAP to predict the strokes in various emergency conditions. From the results, the Proposed CB-FSCAP established better results when compared to existing Random Forest (RF) by providing results in terms of accuracy (98.4%), precision (95.1 %), recall (96.50/0) and F1-score (95.7%) respectively.

articleTitle: Crash Injury Prediction Using Bidirectional Gated Recurrent Unit with Multi Head Attention Network
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Integrated Intelligence and Communication Systems (ICIICS)

authors.preferredName: Rana Veer Samara Sihman Bharattej R

abstract: In this era, Crash injury prediction is a crucial area of research aimed at reducing road traffic mortalities and injuries, which remain a leading global cause of death. Previous researchers have suggested various methods but still there is need to improve the accuracy and reliability of these predictions by analyzing large, multi-dimensional datasets from various sources, road conditions, and driver data. Therefore, this paper suggests an approach to predict the severity of injury occurred during the vehicle crash. Firstly, the data is collected from the Ministry of transport and logistics services. Then, the accumulated data is processed through a sampling technique namely Adaptive Synthetic (ADASYN). The sampled data is embedded into the model combined with correlation based selection with Recursive Feature Elimination (RFE) techniques for extraction of suitable features and selection of optimal attributes based on ranking method. Then based on the selected optimal features, injury prediction is initiated by employing Bidirectional Gated Recurrent Unit (BiGRU) with Multi-head Attention Network (MAN) technique. Finally the overall interpretation of the model is developed by SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP). The proposed model namely BiGRU-MAN-SHAP resulted with 93.63% accuracy.

articleTitle: Integration and Analysis of Network Information System Operation and Maintenance Data Based on Artificial Intelligence Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Integrated Intelligence and Communication Systems (ICIICS)
abstract: Nowadays, the operation and management of network information systems face numerous challenges, especially in data management and analysis. This study aims to improve the data integration and analysis process of network information system operation and maintenance through artificial intelligence(AI) technology. First, the study intelligently classifies and preprocesses operation and maintenance data by applying machine learning(ML) algorithms, extracts key information using natural language processing techniques, and subsequently conducts in-depth data correlation analysis using a deep learning(DL) model, so as to effectively identify potential bottlenecks in the system and early warning failure signals. The aspect of improving the learning rate when parameter tuning increases the accuracy from 88% to 90%, indicating that the faster learning rate helps the model to better adapt to the data, although there may be a risk of overfitting. The findings of this paper will provide new ideas for the operation and maintenance of networked information systems and will be useful for the improvement of the operation quality of other information systems.

Author Keywords: operation and maintenance data integration analysis

articleTitle: Deep Learning Model for Pigeon Pea Leaf Disease Identification
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Integrated Intelligence and Communication Systems (ICIICS)
abstract: The world's main grain crop is pigeon pea. It sustains the mainstream of the world's population with nourishment and liveliness. Various pigeon pea leaf diseases which may occur by fungal, bacterial and viral infections and are major threat to the world's agricultural production because they deteriorate crop quality in addition to lowering crop yield. Traditional strategies of classifying and managing disorders frequently rely on laborious and subjective manual examination procedures. However, recent advancements in computer vision methods have made it possible to construct automated systems that can recognize illnesses from picture data. In this work major leaves spoiled by disorders are classified: leaf spot, sterilic mosaic and leaf webber along with healthy pigeon pea plant leaves. The usefulness of the Convolutional Block Attention Module (CBAM) and squeeze-and-excitation (SE) attention processes are examined in this study. Renowned CNN models, such as ResNet50 and VGG19, are used to perform transfer learning for the categorization of plant diseases and are subsequently improved. The results of this study demonstrate that ResNet50 + CBAM stands out as the superior performer, showcasing remarkable metrics across various evaluation criteria. Interestingly, ResNet attains a noteworthy 0.97 accuracy.

articleTitle: AI-Driven Digital Mirror Technology for Securing IoT-Enabled Smart Infrastructures
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Integrated Intelligence and Communication Systems (ICIICS)
abstract: The expansion of the Internet of Things (IoT) is driven by the proliferation of interconnected wireless gadgets, made possible by ever-improving computer and Internet infrastructure. The IoT is an extensive system of interconnected sensors and gateways. In the course of their constant environmental interaction, IoT devices produce a wealth of data resources, including images, audio, video, digital signals, and more. Connectivity to the Internet allows all Internet of Things (IoT) equipment and apps to exchange data and resources more effectively. The proposed AI-Driven Digital Mirror Technology effectively enhances the security of IoT-enabled smart infrastructures by integrating real-time monitoring, anomaly detection, and adaptive response mechanisms. By employing advanced AI algorithms such as Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) and Reinforcement Learning (RL), the technology mirrors IoT environments digitally, enabling dynamic modeling and threat assessment. The system demonstrated a significant improvement in threat detection accuracy, achieving a precision rate of 95.6% and a recall rate of 93.2% during simulations. Additionally, the adaptive response mechanism reduced the average response time to security breaches by 40%, ensuring minimal disruption to infrastructure operations. Comparative analysis with traditional security solutions highlighted the system's superiority in mitigating complex, multi-layered attacks, and its scalability makes it suitable for various smart infrastructure applications, including smart cities, industrial automation, and intelligent transportation systems. The results underscore the potential of AI-Driven Digital Mirror Technology in securing IoT ecosystems against evolving cyber threats while maintaining operational efficiency and resilience.

articleTitle: Optimizing Brain Tumor Detection with Multi-Head Deep Convolutional Neural Network: An Effective Framework for MRI Based Classification and Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Integrated Intelligence and Communication Systems (ICIICS)
abstract: Various detection techniques are used to find brain tumors, but MRI is the most reliable because of its high image resolution. However, classifying brain tumors manually takes a lot of time. This study suggests a novel method for classifying brain tumors called the Multi-head Deep Convolutional Neural Network (MHDCovNet) Algorithm in order to overcome these difficulties. The Data Pre-processing phase includes improvements like noise reduction, image sharpening, and the removal of non-brain tissues (skull stripping) to guarantee the images are of high quality appropriate for analysis. The above steps are essential for getting images ready for further examination. Important attributes, such as statistical and texture-based features, are extracted from the pre-processed MRI scans in the Feature Extraction phase in order to obtain the information required for classification. A complex Multi-head Deep Convolutional Neural Network (MHDCovNet), which makes use of cutting- edge deep learning features like multi-head attention and global average pooling, is used to achieve the final phase, tumor classification. The effectiveness of the developed technique in classifying brain tumors is then demonstrated by comparing the results with state of the art methods.

articleTitle: Anemia Prediction Using Machine Learning Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Integrated Intelligence and Communication Systems (ICIICS)
abstract: Anemia is a common illness with a major influence on world health, so early detection and treatment for anemia is very much necessary and efficient diagnostic methods are very much required. In addition to other pertinent clinical parameters, analysis of Red Blood Cell (RBC) prints can play a major role in early identification of anemia. RBC prints are analyzed using ML models in this paper, which offers a unique method for anemia prediction using hemoglobin count, percentage of Red, Green and Blue pixels of RBC prints and gender to produce an all-encompassing predictive model. The performance of ML models such as KNN, SVM etc. have been evaluated using cross validation technique by calculating the mean accuracy, f1, precision and recall scores for different folds. The best performing model evaluated through fifteen-fold cross validation is Decision Tree Classifier showing an accuracy of 98.72%.

articleTitle: Age-Adaptive Lung Cancer Prediction Using Ensemble Learning Methods
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Integrated Intelligence and Communication Systems (ICIICS)
abstract: Lung cancer, a leading cause of cancer-related deaths globally, is caused predominantly by smoking. This study compares machine learning (ML) and ensemble learning (EL) models to predict lung cancer across different age groups, high-lighting an age-adaptive approach. Data preprocessing involved handling null values, deduplication, and encoding categorical variables. Key lung cancer risk factors were selected using chi-square tests, and data was divided into young-aged, middle-aged and old-aged cohorts, with standardized scaling applied for computational efficiency. The data point from the young cohort was excluded due to the presence of a singular data instance. Furthermore, due to segregation of cohorts, the data left was imbalanced. To up-sample the imbalanced data, Synthetic Miniority Oversampling Technique (SMOTE) was used. For each machine learning and ensemble learning model, an optimal set of parameters was determined using hyperparameter tuining tool from scikit-learn library - GridSearchCV. Given the limited quantity of data, the models with these selected parameters were then trained using K-Fold Cross Validation to ensure robust performance. The results show that for middle-aged individuals, K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN) and Random Forests (RF) achieved top accuracies of 92.22% and 92.78% respectively, while for old-aged cohorts, Gaussian Naive Bayes (NB) and RF yielded 95.66% and 96.98 %. This age-specific analysis emphasizes the RF model's robustness in predicting lung cancer risk across age brackets.

articleTitle: A Comprehensive Study of Machine Learning and Deep Learning Technique Based Personalized Treatment Analysis Using Electronic Health Records
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Integrated Intelligence and Communication Systems (ICIICS)
abstract: Electronic Health Records (EHR) serves as a digital platform for the storage and maintenance of medical patient history for future analysis. The EHR allows for easy and quick access to patient details, facilitating a better diagnosis by healthcare professionals. The EHR platform improves communication within healthcare, which leads to reduction in medical errors. The EHR data includes details such as medical history, diagnosis, lab and test results, treatment plans, and radiology images that require large datasets. Reducing the dimensionality of data without losing important information is very complex. Hence, Machine Learning (ML) and Deep Learning (DL) methods are used to regulate personalized treatment analysis based on the EHRs. The ML and DL methods employ classification techniques such as Recurrent Neural Network (RNN), Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), Multilayer Perceptron (MLP), Random Forest (RF), Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), Support Vector Machine (SVM), Reinforcement Learning, and Linear Regression (LR) to ensure accurate predictions and formulate personalized treatment plans. The performance metrices such as recall, precision, specificity, and FI-Score are used to evaluate the performance of the proposed model against that of the existing models.

articleTitle: Reliable and Secured Cluster Based Routing in WSN via Lyrebird-Panda Optimization Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Integrated Intelligence and Communication Systems (ICIICS)
abstract: Routing and clustering approaches can assist address the primary issue of dependable energy-aware data transmission in wireless sensor networks (WSN). Data transmission's use in WSN situations has grown recently due to its dynamic nature. However, WSNs face a number of difficulties when sending data, such as a shorter network lifetime, lower EE, and a worse level of security. This study develops a new cluster head selection model for WSN. In this case, a new technique called Red Panda Incorporated Lyrebird Optimization (RPI-LBO) is used to elect the CHs in the best possible way. Energy, link longevity, link quality, security, and trust are all taken into account when performing the CHS. The link lifetime for 100 nodes using RPI-LBO is 42 from the 1200th to the 1800th round. However, the suggested RPI-LBO revealed a longer connection lifetime than the examined LBO, RPA, WaOA, SBOA, and COA schemes for all node counts.

articleTitle: Node Localization Performance Evaluation and Tracking using Kalman Filter in Wireless Sensor Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Integrated Intelligence and Communication Systems (ICIICS)
abstract: Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs) are crucial in smart environments where precise node location is necessary for efficient data processing and communication. Present-day localization methods frequently provide an average accuracy of about 11.3%, which degrades network performance as a whole. The proposed research work presents a hybrid method to increase localization accuracy by merging the Kalman Filter (KF) with Random Fourier Feature (RFF) and Support Vector Machine (SVM). By using the RFF for feature mapping and the KF for effective tracking, this technique greatly lowers localization errors. The Mean Absolute Error(MAE) reduced from 7.74 to 3.87 for the first trajectory, 8.41 to 4.31 for the second, and 9.47 to 8.31 for the third trajectory. By improving WSN's accuracy and dependability, the suggested method increases their usefulness in intelligent applications.

articleTitle: Forecasting of Groundwater Quality Utilizing an Efficient K-Means with Principal Component Analysis Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Integrated Intelligence and Communication Systems (ICIICS)
abstract: Groundwater stands as a pivotal freshwater resource in numerous regions worldwide, but the burgeoning population and diverse economic activities have adversely impacted its quality. However, the K-means algorithm is sensitive to the initial placement of centroids, where outliers can significantly influence the position of centroids resulting in suboptimal clusters. To address this, it is recommended to remove or clip outliers before applying K-means scales well to large datasets making it suitable for handling substantial amounts of data. In this proposed method, attributes are first calculated using Principal Component Analysis (PCA) determines the weight of each attribute based on eigenvalues. The PCA, by determining attribute weights and Rapid Centroid Estimation (RCE), by establishing the initial cluster centre, contribute to the overall effectiveness of the method. The classification step utilizes a Linear Support Vector Machine (SVM), suitable for linear hyper line data when the dataset can be classified into two classes using a single straight line. The results obtained showcase the superiority of the proposed method, achieving a Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE) of 1.23, R-squared (R2) of 0.90, Mean Absolute Deviation (MAD) of 0.28 and E of 0.97 on the Indian groundwater dataset. These outcomes affirm better detection and classification performance compared to other existing methods, such as Random Forest (RF), Decision Tree (DT) and K-Nearest Neighbour (KNN).

Author Keywords: k-means with principal component analyst and linear support vector machine

articleTitle: Energy Efficient Clustering in Wireless Sensor Networks: A Grey Wolf-based TEEN Protocol
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Integrated Intelligence and Communication Systems (ICIICS)
abstract: Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs) are pivotal for various applications, but they face significant challenges, primarily due to the limited battery life of sensor nodes. The clustering of sensor nodes is a key research domain within WSNs, aimed at improving energy efficiency by organizing nodes into clusters and optimizing Cluster Head (CH) selection. Efficient CH selection is crucial for balancing the network load and extending its lifespan. Hence, in this paper, the challenge of CH selection is addressed by proposing an enhanced method that leverages the Grey Wolf Optimization (GWO) algorithm, incorporating node centrality into the fitness function. Additionally, the data transmission is optimized using the Threshold-sensitive Energy Efficient Network (TEEN) protocol to minimize data redundancy and improve overall energy efficiency. The proposed GWO-TEEN approach achieves a mean energy consumption of 27.58, outperforming other methods such as I-GWO (78.22), FI-GWO (148.74), and F-PSO (191.41), demonstrating its effectiveness in enhancing energy efficiency and network longevity.

articleTitle: Japanese Dependency Analysis using Multi-Kernel Support Vector Machine based on Term Frequency and Inverse Document Frequency
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Integrated Intelligence and Communication Systems (ICIICS)
abstract: Nowadays, Japanese dependency analysis examines the grammatical structure of sentences and identifies the relations between words and phrases of text. This analysis is involving with natural language processing (NLP) with in dependency analysis is particularly important due to its complex sentence structure and grammatical relations. However, dependency analysis is the complexity of handling long-distance dependencies and nested clauses, which can lead to accuracy issues and increased computational requirements. To overcome those issues this research proposes an ensemble model of Multi-Kernel Support Vector Machine (MK-SVM) for Japanese dependency analysis. Initially the data is collected from the Japanese Text Dataset (JTD). The dataset is preprocessed through normalization, stemming, and stop-words removal, followed by feature extraction using Term Frequency-Inverse Document Frequency (TF-IDF) and N-grams. The preprocessed data is then classified using MK-SVM, which combines multiple kernel functions to improve accuracy. By leveraging the strengths of different kernels, MK-SVM enhances classification performance. The proposed MK-SVM model is used to overcome drawbacks of existing system terms of metrices the values are of 97.01 % of precision, 96.01 % of recall, 98.96% of F1 score and 96.82% of accuracy, when compared to the existing method like k-nearest neighbors (KNN) respectively.

articleTitle: Integrated Algorithm of Stacking and its Application in Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Integrated Intelligence and Communication Systems (ICIICS)
abstract: Ensemble learning constructs and combines multiple learners to complete learning tasks. This paper studies the XGBoost model, logistic regression model, and LightGBM model based on the integrated Stacking algorithm model. XGBoost model can further realize the cross combination of features through serial results, and obtain the global optimal parameter combination within the grid parameters. Logistic regression model to analyze the predicted value of all types of data, including continuous variables, discrete variables and dummy variables, without considering the prior probability loss; the LightGBM model filters the original features using the LightGBM feature selection algorithm, and then truncates the feature variables according to different threshold conditions. In order to verify the applicability of the integrated Stacking algorithm model constructed in this paper, student learning behavior features were constructed, and Pearson coefficient was used to calculate the correlation between the features. The experimental results show that the prediction model constructed with the integrated Stacking algorithm can meet the requirements of predicting scores in universities.

articleTitle: Integration of Heuristic-Based Weighted Feature Fusion Concept for Multi-Focus Image Fusion Model
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Integrated Intelligence and Communication Systems (ICIICS)
abstract: Background of the study: In particular, images only focus on a portion of the scene and only capture particular details because of the limited depth of the image-capturing device. Methods: An effective Multi-Focus Image Fusion (MFIF) model is designed. The MF images are gathered from benchmark sources. The collected images are given into Discrete Wavelet Transform (DWT) for dividing the images into high-frequency sub-bands as well as low-frequency sub-bands. Further, the weighted feature fusion is performed, whereas the weight optimization takes place using Grey Wolf Optimization (GWO). Further, the IDWT on the fused images helps to attain final fused multi-focus image. Results achieved: By considering the BRISQUE analysis, the developed model outperforms 11.11%, 57%, 12.2%, and 17.4% enhanced than RTH-DWT, RPOA-DWT, KOA-DWT, and GRO-DWT in terms of best analysis. Concluding remarks: Thus, the experimental analysis of the developed model has shown effective and superior performance.

articleTitle: Omnichannel Marketing Strategies: Bridging the Gap Between Online and Offline Retail Experiences Using DCNN-BiLSTM Technique
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Integrated Intelligence and Communication Systems (ICIICS)
abstract: Omnichannel marketing, in which several channels are integrated to provide consumers with a consistent service experience, is an essential part of multichannel management, and companies have come to appreciate this. Despite the widespread adoption of omnichannel initiatives, little is known regarding the factors that impact integration quality (INQ) across all channels. The system uses research on omni and multi-channel services to establish and validate the quality dimensions and sub-dimensions of omnichannel integration. The proposed approach incorporates preprocessing, feature selection, and training of the model. The preprocessing step is crucial since the model's accuracy and performance are directly affected by the quality of the training data. In feature selection, words are embedded. The DCNN-BiLSTM model was consistently used throughout the whole training procedure. With a mean accuracy of 92.58%, this innovative method surpasses DCNN and LSTM.

articleTitle: Intelligent E-Commerce Marketing System Based on Mobile Multi Agent
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Integrated Intelligence and Communication Systems (ICIICS)
abstract: Currently, research on intelligent mobile agents in the field of e-commerce is mostly still in the theoretical and mathematical argumentation stage, while actual research and system development are still in the initial stage, and there are also problems such as low information acquisition efficiency. This article proposes a design approach for an Agent based e-commerce intelligent agent by addressing the shortcomings of existing research on the application of intelligent mobile agents in e-commerce. It aims to provide users and merchants with more convenient services, reduce the burden of network bandwidth, improve information retrieval speed. In the comparison of customer returns before and after the adoption of a mobile Multi Agent intelligent e-commerce marketing system, the data collection time is one month, and the maximum return before the adoption can reach 49 orders. After adoption, the maximum return quantity is 10 orders, and sometimes the return quantity is 0. This article helps to improve the level of e-commerce transaction management.

articleTitle: Early Detection of College Student Mental Health Issues Using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Integrated Intelligence and Communication Systems (ICIICS)
abstract: This paper explores using machine learning to create early warning models that identify college students at risk for mental health issues like depression and anxiety. By analyzing data such as academic performance, demographics, campus involvement, and digital activity, we aim to proactively connect at-risk students with mental health resources. We apply both supervised and unsupervised techniques, including classification, clustering, and neural networks, to a dataset from a large public university. The best-performing model, random forest, achieved 81% accuracy in identifying students with risk factors for depression and anxiety. Clustering analysis revealed common patterns of academic struggles, social isolation, and addictive digital behavior among at-risk groups. These findings highlight the potential for machine learning to support early intervention and improve student well-being and success. Future work will focus on refining the models, expanding to additional campuses, and integrating predictive tools with university mental health strategies.

articleTitle: Musical Instrument Classification Using Deep Learning CNN Models
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Integrated Intelligence and Communication Systems (ICIICS)
abstract: Musical instrument recognition is the act of counting on machine learning or the application of signal processing to isolate and classify various musical instruments in an audio track. Such capability makes it possible to better analyze musical pieces, which may be helpful whenever features need to be transcribed, songs recommended, or when they need to be composed automatically. In this work, we put forward a CNN based model for musical instruments classification using the FreeSound dataset. The model performs Mel-spectrograms on extracted audio inputs and make use of a highly effective data augmentation methodology known as CutMix. By using hyperparameter tuning and pruning approaches, the model configuration and structure is improved thereby enabling its effectiveness. Further, Class Activation Maps and an Ablation Study are employed to analyse interpretability and uncover the strength of the technique in instrument recognition. The accuracy was at 85%; the use of a richer database and convolutional neural networks may lift the accuracy of the classification. Using this algorithm means its application in a wider context of sound classification is possible and at some point, the algorithm can learn beyond a human's capability to differentiate between similar sounds (for example, distinguishing between viola and violin, which humans cannot do). Real world applications of musical instrument recognition are numerous. It can make the sorting and searching of enormous musical libraries possible with great efficiency, which would be valuable to streaming services since these offer their users relevant tune recommendations.

articleTitle: Urban Sound Classification with Convolutional Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Integrated Intelligence and Communication Systems (ICIICS)
abstract: Tremendous population and urban growth rates all over the present potent threats to create livable and sustainable cities. It leads to the extension and transformation of urban noises, and the diversification of the latter is attributed to this increase. These sounds they turned into is still regarded more as noise than as actual information which is an important factor in the smart cities idea. This research seeks to establish whether it is possible to enhance the classification of urban sounds by adopting CNNs for sound recognition to help improve the safety of pedestrians by identifying possible danger sounds. According to the data, traffic injuries of pedestrians are escalating around the world, partly because of a lack of sensitivity to the surroundings. This work intends to categorize urban sounds, for instance sirens or noise produced by vehicles in real time so as to enlighten the pedestrian of close dangers, hence avoiding mishaps. The deep learning model built in this context is made up of three convolutional layers having a max pooling layer to improve the model's feature extracting ability and final classification accuracy with the GlobalAveragePooling2D layer. In this context, the performance of the model was assessed with UrbanSound8k, which consists of more than 8,700 urban audio samples, thus allowing for reliable performance analysis. Findings show that the model is quite effective at separating sounds commonly encountered in urban settings and reaffirms an intended use of the model which is to aid pedestrian safety. This research focuses on utilizing CNN-based audio classification in real-time hazard detection with possible extension to enhance urban safety and additional usage of sound-based alarms.

articleTitle: Cau-Net: Enhancing Medical Image Segmentation With Contour-Guided Attention for Accurate Stroke Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Integrated Intelligence and Communication Systems (ICIICS)
abstract: Accurate segmentation of medical images is necessary for accurate diagnosis and treatment planning. The achievement of the precise boundaries in complex anatomical structures is difficult. In this paper, a novel hybrid segmentation model called Contour-Guided Attention U-Net (CAU-Net) is proposed by combining the traditional region-based active contour models with the advanced deep learning capabilities of Attention U-Net. CAU-Net employs an active contour model that generates an initial segmentation mask that provides the boundary awareness needed to steer the attention U-Net refinement. The use of attention mechanisms will be allowed with the selective features on the regions of interest identified by active contours in order to refine it to high accuracy of results in segmentation. It was tested on a Kaggle MRI dataset of medical images, including stroke prediction tasks, and performed better in boundary accuracy and overall segmentation quality than standalone Attention U-Net and active contour models. In stroke prediction, the CAU-Net achieved 98.3% segmentation accuracy and a Dice coefficient of 0.87 in detecting stroke lesions and delineating fine anatomical details. From the results, the hybrid approach significantly amplifies the contour adherence in addition to contextual sensitivity such that these are effective methods in such complex segmentation task especially those in medical applications.

articleTitle: Sensor Data Fusion Algorithm and its Application Effect Evaluation in Greenhouse Environment
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Integrated Intelligence and Communication Systems (ICIICS)
abstract: In today's rapidly developing modern agriculture, agricultural intelligence has gradually become an important way to improve the yield and quality of agricultural products. To solve this problem, this article intends to adopt a multi-sensor information fusion method to achieve real-time monitoring of the indoor environment. This article uses a combination of Kalman filtering and Bayesian estimation to weight the information from multiple sensors, in order to reduce the error of a single sensor and obtain more accurate environmental parameters. Based on this, experiments are conducted in real greenhouse environments to comprehensively evaluate the application effect of the algorithm. Within a week, the temperature remained relatively stable, with an average temperature ranging from 23 °C to 25 °C. This slight change indicates that this method can ensure the continuity and stability of the data. The research results will help improve the accuracy and reliability of greenhouse environmental monitoring, and provide scientific basis for agricultural production management.

articleTitle: Wireless Capsule Endoscopy for Crohn's Disease Automated Image Classification Using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Integrated Intelligence and Communication Systems (ICIICS)
abstract: Despite the diagnosis of Crohn's Disease now transformed through wireless capsule endoscopy (WCE), traditional manual interpretation by gastroenterologists contains substantial restrictions such as high inter-observer inconsistency, time dedication, and potential oversight of important clinical signs. The paper proposes an automated image classification system founded on deep learning methods specifically, Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) for feature extraction and Long Short-Term Memory networks (LSTM) for temporal sequence examination. The technique applies Transfer Learning to improve model performance with minimal labeled data, thus facilitating precise identification of CD-related abnormalities. Strong testing on an endoscopist-annotated dataset indicates the proposed system substantially surpasses existing systems about accuracy of 94.5%, sensitivity of 92.0%, and specificity of 96.0%. Promising enhanced patient outcomes in the therapy of Crohn's Disease, the automated method significantly decreases interpretation time, minimizes inter-observer inconsistency, and increases diagnostic accuracy.

articleTitle: Application of Natural Gradient Boosting and Grid Search in Fault Detection and Diagnosis of Electrical Power Grids
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Integrated Intelligence and Communication Systems (ICIICS)
abstract: In recent years, the demand of electrical power grids had increased tremendously since; girds are primary sources for meeting the electricity demand. However, due to occurrence of faults continuously the power grids are failing in providing constant supply. Several methods are employed for detecting the faults but they failed in effectively classifying types of faults. Therefore, this research proposes Natural Gradient Boosting and Grid Search (NGBoost-Grid Search) for detection and diagnosis of electric faults in electrical power grid. Initially, the data is taken from publicly available electric fault line detection dataset. Then, these current signals are pre-processed by using Interquartile Range (IQR), Hilbert Huang Transformation (HHT) and min-max normalization. After that, Elastic Net technique is employed for selecting the optimal features from pre-processed signals for eliminating irrelevant signals. Finally, selected optimal features are classified by using NGBoost for distinguishing the fault current signals and healthy current signals, Grid search is integrated to hyper tune for improving the performance of NGBoost and gave effective classification of fault and normal current signals. The proposed NGBoost-Grid Search achieved attained better results such as accuracy (96.47%), precision (97.63%), Recall (89.94%) and Fl-score (93.29%) respectively when compared with existing Support Vector Machine (SVM).

articleTitle: Accurate Precipitation Prediction Model Based on Deep Learning Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Integrated Intelligence and Communication Systems (ICIICS)
abstract: In the context of global climate change, extreme weather events occur frequently, causing serious impacts on society, economy, and people's lives. Therefore, improving the accuracy of precipitation forecasting is of great significance. This article intends to combine multi-source weather information with long short-term memory networks to propose a deep learning based precipitation accurate prediction model, which can accurately describe the temporal and spatial distribution of rainfall events. The error rate shows regional differences, for example, the error rate for predicting heatwaves in Europe is as low as 10%, while the error rate for predicting droughts in Africa is as high as 18%. The research results of this article will help improve the accuracy of rainfall forecasting and provide new ideas and methods for using deep learning for complex weather forecasting in disaster prevention and reduction, agricultural planning, water management, and other areas.

articleTitle: Application of Machine Vision Technology in Intelligent Recognition Devices for Miscellaneous Objects
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Integrated Intelligence and Communication Systems (ICIICS)
abstract: This paper proposes a machine vision technology solution based on RCIR camera to address the difficulty of intelligent identification of impurities in tobacco sorting. Firstly, choose RCIR camera as the main image acquisition device, and enhance the recognition ability of complex backgrounds and substances with similar colors by combining the three spectral channels of red, cyan, and infrared. Subsequently, a series of image preprocessing methods were employed, including Gaussian filtering, histogram equalization, and image normalization, to enhance image quality and resolution. Then, by extracting shape, color, and texture features, a support vector machine (SVM) classifier is used to accurately distinguish between tobacco and miscellaneous items. The experimental results show that the average recognition accuracy of RCIR cameras is 92%, which is 7 percentage points higher than the 85% of traditional RGB cameras; The recall rate has increased from 82% for RGB to 90%; Meanwhile, the processing speed has been reduced from 1.6 seconds for RGB cameras to 1.1 seconds. The experimental results verified the significant advantages of the machine vision system based on RCIR camera in recognition accuracy, efficiency, and production line automation level, highlighting its potential application in tobacco sorting.

articleTitle: A Few-Shot Learning-Based Domain-Adaptive Lightweight CNN for Robust Hand Gesture Recognition in Real-Time Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Integrated Intelligence and Communication Systems (ICIICS)
abstract: Surface electromyogram-based hand gesture recognition (sEMG) has promising prospects in human-machine interaction applications, including the neural rehabilitation and assistive technologies. However, this technique also has several disadvantages, such as poor generalization across subj ects and days, demanding a large amount of data for calibration, and computational complexity that does not enable the real-time deployment of the system. The proposed work incorporates a novel few-shot learning-based domain-adaptive lightweight CNN that is specifically designed to be used in robust and efficient hand gesture recognition. This minimizes the dependency on the labeled data of other new subj ects or days, hence allowing better adaptability in real-world scenarios. The proposed lightweight CNN architecture adapts well to wearable devices with real-time performance but high accuracy. Another would be adding domain-adaptive feature learning to account for variations between inter-subject and inter-day domains while preserving the accuracy of classification and improving model generalization. The proposed framework is able to achieve competitive accuracy using a small calibration set in gesture-based human-machine interfaces continuously and broadly. Results on high-density sEM G datasets have shown that our model achieves a good balance between the accuracy (95.5<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>) and efficiency on experimental results and holds promise for providing a reliable solution for real-time cross-domain hand gesture recognition applications.

articleTitle: Advancing Chronic Kidney Disease Detection: Improving Biomarkers and CT Imaging for Enhanced Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Integrated Intelligence and Communication Systems (ICIICS)
abstract: Chronic Kidney Disease (CKD) is one of the biggest health concerns globally, affecting millions. This research aims to enhance the early detection and diagnosis of CKD by utilizing advanced machine-learning models for two different types of data: biomarkers and CT scan images. Each model has been trained and then individually validated. The Random Forest model has given the best average accuracy of 99.4% using different cross-validation methods while the CNN model has reached a validation accuracy of 99.41 %, showing minimum overfitting in each. Thus, both of these models can offer a high level of improvement in accuracy in the detection of CKD if applied separately. Future studies are needed to identify how these models can be incorporated into clinical practice for the betterment of early diagnosis and enhanced patient outcomes.

articleTitle: Gated Recurrent Unit Based Deep Learning Model For Bitcoin Price Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Integrated Intelligence and Communication Systems (ICIICS)
abstract: Over the years, the fluctuations of price of Bitcoin creates many challenges for the data scientists and market investors in predicting the accurate price of bitcoin. In past, many researchers have implemented different models to predict the price of Bitcoin, but still it is required improvement in accurate prediction. In the present study, we proposed the Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU) model to forecast the accurate price of bitcoin. All the models are experimented using the Yahoo Finance dataset, and the performance of the proposed GRU model is explored with six different deep learning models as Additive Prophet, Multiplicative Prophet, Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (BiLSTM), CatBooster, Support Vector Regression (SVR), and hybrid GRU 1D-CNN. The model evaluation is performed based on various metrics such as Mean Absolute Error (MAE), Root Mean Square Error (RMSE), and R2 score. From the experimental analysis it is observed that, the performance of the GRU model is outperformed over it's counterparts and produced better result with more prediction reliability.

articleTitle: Signal Detection and Classification in Communication Network Using Quadrature Amplitude Modulation with Signal to Noise Ratio
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Integrated Intelligence and Communication Systems (ICIICS)

authors.preferredName: Rana Veer Samara Sihman Brahmatej Rupavath

abstract: In recent years, signal detection in the telecommunication networks automated dependent radio frequency for aircraft identification and verification with emotion recognition, radar and biomedical systems. However, the existing Deep Learning (DL) based techniques failed to interact and detect noise and dynamic environments. To overcome the problem, a Quadrature Amplitude Modulation and Signal-to-Noise Ratio (QAM-SNR) method is proposed for digital communication and signal detection of both the amplitude and phase of carrier signal. The proposed QAM-SNR method is developed on Dataset for Emotion Analysis using Psychological signals (DEAP) dataset, which consists of electromyogram and electrooculogram for signal detection in stimuli using Low-Pass Filter for detection. Then, the preprocessed data of detection in signal is extracted using Generative Adversarial Network and Spiking Neural Network (GAN-SNN) for enhanced detection with improved robustness to adversarial attacks. Finally, QAM-SNR is employed for efficient use of bandwidth in detection of the signals for communication networks with high quality of results. Experimental results of the proposed QAM-SNR method attained accuracy (99.70%), precision (99.78%), F1-score (99.87%) are higher than existing detection techniques such as Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) and Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (Bi-LSTM).

articleTitle: An Optimal Storage Cyber Security for Block-Chain-Assisted WSN: Identifying Malicious Nodes and Enhancing the Storage of Data
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Integrated Intelligence and Communication Systems (ICIICS)
abstract: Wireless sensor networks (WSN), an crucial part of the Internet of Things (IoT), are utilized in cybersecurity, healthcare, and military applications but face challenges like resource limitations and rogue nodes, which affect security. This study proposes a WSN architecture with three types of nodes: base stations (BSs), cluster heads (CHs), and sensor nodes (SNs). SNs collect data, which CHs process and send to BSs. Both SNs and CHs register using blockchain with the Practical Byzantine Fault Tolerance (PBFT) consensus for authentication and data security. After registration, nodes transmit data securely to BSs. The WSN dataset (WSN-DS) with min-max normalization is used, and a new method, ε-insensitive two-plane support vector regression (ε-TSVR), identifies malicious nodes. The findings show the proposed method improves accuracy (91%), f1 score (93%), recall (94%), and precision (92%), offering a more secure WSN solution for IoT environments, even with malicious nodes.

articleTitle: Design of Interactive 3D Virtual System for Products Based on Machine Vision
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Integrated Intelligence and Communication Systems (ICIICS)
abstract: With the rapid development of virtual reality (VR) and augmented reality (AR) technologies, interactive 3D virtual systems have been widely used in fields such as industrial design, medical simulation, and education and training. However, existing 3D virtual interaction systems still have shortcomings in multimodal interaction collaboration and adaptability to application scenarios. This article studies a visual perception based design framework that utilizes machine vision technology to achieve multimodal interactions such as gesture recognition, posture perception, and eye tracking. By combining convolutional neural networks (CNN), 3D scene modeling, and real-time rendering technology, the naturalness of interactions and the real-time feedback capability of the system are improved. The system architecture consists of three modules: visual perception, virtual environment, and user interaction, supporting users to manipulate objects in the roaming scene through natural actions. To validate the system, the study compared visual perception with traditional interaction methods through experiments, collected data on user response time, accuracy, and satisfaction, and analyzed the stability and feedback fluency of the system. The results show that compared with traditional interaction methods, machine vision based 3D virtual systems have task completion times within 10 seconds and system stability exceeding 90%. The experimental results show that the 3D virtual interaction system based on visual perception has significant advantages in improving interaction efficiency, user immersion, and multimodal interaction coordination. This study provides new ideas for future applications in fields such as education, entertainment, and industrial design.

articleTitle: Optimizing Consumer Insights: Predicting Customer Purchase Behavior by Using Artificial Neural Networks Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Integrated Intelligence and Communication Systems (ICIICS)
abstract: This study investigates the use of artificial neural networks (ANN) to predict consumer purchase behavior based on behavioral and demographic characteristics. The proposed ANN model comprises input, hidden, and output layers, optimized through hyperparameter tuning for improved prediction accuracy. The model employs non-linear activation functions, including ReLU, Sigmoid, and Tanh, alongside both Stochastic Gradient Descent (SGD) and Adam optimizers to enhance learning efficiency. Results indicate that Adam and RMSprop optimizers achieve the best balance, with Adam providing the highest accuracy (0.88) and RMSprop showing the lowest loss (0.2614) with strong accuracy (0.87), making these optimizers well-suited for capturing complex consumer behavior patterns. Further accuracy, loss, confusion matrix, ROC curve, and area under the curve (AUC)-demonstrate the model's capacity to capture intricate patterns. The confusion matrix highlights high precision in classification, with an overall accuracy of correctly predicting 262 out of 300 cases. The ROC curve further supports the model's classification strength, achieving an AUC of 0.92, which confirms its high discriminatory ability. These findings suggest the ANN model is effective for deriving consumer insights, capable of delivering accurate forecasts for data-driven marketing strategies and customer behavior optimization in practical business settings.

articleTitle: A DL-DeNoiseNet Framework for Robust Image Denoising and Artifact Reduction in Medical Image Diagnostics
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Integrated Intelligence and Communication Systems (ICIICS)
abstract: For precise illness diagnosis and therapy planning, medical imaging diagnostics are necessary. Nevertheless, diagnostic errors can occur due to noise and aberrations that are inherent to imaging modalities including CT, MRI, and ultrasound, which can hide important features. In order to overcome this obstacle, we present a medical diagnostics-specific framework for deep learning-based picture denoising and artifact reduction. Our method improves feature extraction while maintaining picture integrity by combining a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) with a Residual Dense Block (RDB). To guarantee optimal performance across varying degrees of noise and image types, the framework is trained on a broad dataset of medical photos, which includes images that are artifact-laden and noisy. A combination of supervised and adversarial learning techniques is used for this purpose. Adaptive filtering for preprocessing, the CNN-RDB network for denoising, and a refinement module that uses perceptual loss to keep things clinically relevant for postprocessing are the three primary steps in the methodology. The model outperforms traditional denoising methods when tested on various medical imaging metrics, including a PSNR of 40.3 dB and an SSIM of 0.97. Furthermore, the suggested architecture successfully mitigates artifacts by an average of 35% as assessed by the Normalized Root Mean Squared Error (NRMSE), guaranteeing that essential diagnostic characteristics are preserved. The results show that the model can improve image clarity, which means that diagnoses can be made more accurately and fewer scans are needed. Better healthcare outcomes are a direct result of the substantial enhancements to picture quality that this framework provides to physicians and radiologists.

articleTitle: An AI-Driven Framework for Personalized Diet Generation and Nutrition Suggestions Using Machine Learning, Computer Vision and NLP
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Integrated Intelligence and Communication Systems (ICIICS)
abstract: To counteract unhealthy eating habits among the younger generation, a novel and economical AI-powered framework has been developed to serve as a virtual nutritionist and nutrition counsellor. The system uses machine learning, computer vision, and natural language processing to provide personalized nutrition plans via an easy-to-use online application. It generates tailored meal plans that consider user preferences, allergies, and meal times by calculating Body Mass Index (BMI) based on user input. In addition to blog links and tailored training regimens (enhanced by the LLM3 model trained on a Kaggle gym dataset), a feedback mechanism allows for continuous optimization. Real-time food classification uses VGG16 and ResNet deep learning models to detect damaged or harmful foods and send out alerts for unsuitable foods. Additionally, integration with Google Maps and KNN helps users locate nearby dietitians, fostering better access to professional guidance. These comprehensive improvements significantly contribute to maintaining a good diet.

articleTitle: Optimization of Corner Gas Accumulation Processing Method Based on Improved Wavelet Threshold and BiLSTM
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Integrated Intelligence and Communication Systems (ICIICS)
abstract: Nowadays, mine gas management is facing increasing challenges, especially the accumulation of corner gas, which poses a great threat to the safety production of miners. This study proposes a Bidirectional Long Short Term Memory (BiLSTM) model based on improved wavelet thresholding for optimizing the detection and processing of mine corner gas. Firstly, by improving the wavelet thresholding method to denoise the gas concentration data, the quality and processing efficiency of the data have been enhanced; next, the BiLSTM model is used to learn and predict the processed data, in order to accurately identify the risk areas of gas accumulation. During the 6-month experimental period, the prediction accuracy of the BiLSTM model remained within the range of 92.5% to 93.3%, with little fluctuation. This article not only optimizes the treatment method of mine corner gas, but also provides a new technical solution for gas safety management.

articleTitle: Protein-Ligand Interaction Prediction with Effective Method of Graph Attention Networks and Long Short-Term Memory
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Integrated Intelligence and Communication Systems (ICIICS)
abstract: Nowadays, the drug discovery field of molecules in protein-ligand interactions developing effective therapeutics for identifying potential drug candidates with spatial features to predict binding affinity. However, the existing Deep Learning (DL) based prediction approaches failed to interact and predict the binding affinity of protein-ligand precisely for drug design with binding affinity. To overcome this problem, a Graph Attention Networks with Long Short-Term Memory (GATN-LSTM) method is proposed with spatiotemporal forecasting for interaction between protein and ligand in binding affinity prediction for drug design. The proposed GATN-LSTM method is employed on DUD-E dataset consists of enhanced the prediction by capturing relationship (interaction) between protein and ligand in molecules for drug discovery using PubChem for prediction. Then, the preprocessed data of protein-ligand interaction is extracted using (CNN-GNN) for better generalization of both local and global features for predicting drug discovery. Finally, GATN-LSTM is employed for interaction of molecules with binding affinity which enhanced the drug design and also improved the prediction results. Experimental results of the proposed GATN-LSTM method attained accuracy (0.9992), F1-score (0.9985) are higher than existing prediction approaches such as Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) and Mutual Information-based Feature Selection (MIFS).

articleTitle: SHAP-Driven Interpretability of Autism Risk in Pregnancy Using Explainable AI
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Integrated Intelligence and Communication Systems (ICIICS)
abstract: Explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) has gained growing popularity for its ability to explain how deep learning and machine learning models make decisions. The frameworks for SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) and Local Interpretable Model-Agnostic Explanations (LIME) have become interpretive tools for ML models. This research closely examines the application of LIME and SHAP in the interpretation of autism spectrum disorder (ASD) detection. It stresses XAI's important role in making AI-based ASD predictions more accurate. Researchers also identified risk factors related to ASD by analyzing the impact of features on it. SHAP shows the TG, AGE, and LDL emerge as the primary features contributing to the prediction of ASD. LIME predicts each patient with 55% confidence in having ASD. The study's findings suggest that machine learning approaches can offer accurate forecasts of ASD status, with the suggested model capable of diagnosing it in its early phases.

articleTitle: Enhanced Stock Market Trend Prediction on the Indonesia Stock Exchange Using Improved Bacterial Foraging Optimization and Elitist Whale Optimization Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Integrated Intelligence and Communication Systems (ICIICS)
abstract: It was difficult to find low-risk firms in 2022 due to the large number of 825 listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX). Essential concerns in financial works include stock price forecasting and price movement forecast. The stock market research has shown encouraging outcomes in the past. We still don't have a consensus on the finest stock value forecasting classical due to the fact that each study report has different architecture and uses different stock issuers. This paper presents a new method for optimizing bacterial foraging that uses optimal deep learning to forecast stock market trends. For the prediction process, the given model employs a multiplicative long short term memory (MLSTM) perfect, with IBFO serving as the model's fine-tuner. The research paper presents a modified whale optimization technique for feature selection. This research proposes an elitist whale optimization algorithm with the nonlinear parameter (EWOANP) to fix the issue where the whale optimization procedure does not strike a balance among exploration and exploitation and instead falls into the local optimum. To improve the odds of evading the local optimum, the shrinking encircling mechanism employs an elitist tactic based on random Cauchy mutation. Using the random Cauchy mutation as a starting point, the method cleverly selects the population with the best mutation solutions to move on to the next iteration. To strike a compromise among the two, the logarithmic spiral mechanism makes use of a nonlinear parameter. There are 2,588,451 entries in the dataset representing 727 IDX firms' open, highest, lowest, closed, and volume transactions. Various stock time records are used to examine the trial findings using current methodologies in terms of distinct metrics.

articleTitle: Enhancing Consumer Sentiment Analysis and Product Improvement with Aspect-Optimized Adaptive GCN (AOA-GCN)
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Integrated Intelligence and Communication Systems (ICIICS)
abstract: The exponential growth in online reviews offers a company the most precious source of information regarding the customers' emotions and potential product improvement areas. However, it is very challenging to derive meaningful information from the unstructured data. The work presents a new model called Aspect-Optimized Adaptive GCN (AOA-GCN), which combines hierarchical structuring with aspect-based optimization for effective consumer sentiment analysis. The AOA-GCN applies a two-level analysis framework that covers both global sentiments and detailed aspect-specific sentiments in order to build a full understanding of the customer review. The model is essentially based on an Adaptive Lightweight GCN with pruning techniques, ensuring that it does not only reduce computations but also takes into account influential aspects along with its high accuracy, even across extended datasets. Dynamic attention in AOA-GCN will help make critical product features in the customer reviews focus on the issues so improvements can be made on those products specifically. Experimental results show that the improved performance is actually as high as 6.45% over global sentiment classification, 9.12% over aspect-based sentiment analysis, and 7.35<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup> over cross-domain generalization, and training time is reduced by 35%. The model also exhibits improved interpretability with clearer insights into customer preferences. The proposed AOA-GCN becomes an effective, efficient, and interpretable business tool for optimizing products through insights from consumers.

articleTitle: The Impact of Influencer Marketing on Consumer Purchasing Decisions in the Digital Age Based on Prophet ARIMA-LSTM Model
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Integrated Intelligence and Communication Systems (ICIICS)
abstract: Many companies still fail to see the value of influencer marketing, star ratings, and customer reviews due to ignorance and a lack of understanding. Researchers are interested in the topic of The Relevance of Influencer Marketing, Ratings and Customer Reviews on Purchasing Decisions because it shows how important it is to have a strategy that combines influencer marketing with positive customer interactions and a good product reputation to influence consumer purchasing decisions. Preprocessing, feature extraction, and model training are all part of the suggested method. Additional measures were taken to guarantee the data's accuracy and relevancy during the SQL data preprocessing phase. Word bags, TF-IDF, and chi-square are the building blocks of feature extraction. During the whole training process, the Prophet-ARIMA-LSTM model was continually employed. This novel approach outperforms ARIMA and LSTM with an average accuracy of 92.72%.

articleTitle: Study on the Operation Optimization of Hybrid Energy Storage System Counting Lithium-ion-liquid Current Batteries
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Integrated Intelligence and Communication Systems (ICIICS)
abstract: In response to the diverse time-span energy storage demands, a hybrid energy storage system operation optimization strategy that integrates lithium-ion and liquid-fluid batteries is proposed. The strategy begins with a thorough examination of the operational mechanisms and energy storage traits of lithium-ion batteries and all-vanadium liquid current batteries, emphasizing their synergistic roles in energy management. Following this, a dual-layer optimization model for the hybrid energy storage system is meticulously devised and streamlined into a unified mixed-integer linear programming framework, leveraging the Karush-Kuhn-Tucker (KKT) condition to ensure a robust solution approach. To validate the model, a case study at a scenic base in Qinghai Province is conducted, quantifying operational enhancements under diverse scenarios. The analysis reveals a post-implementation increase in total revenue by 5.47%, and a notable reduction in wind and solar curtailment by 23.38%, underscoring the economic and operational merits of the hybrid system and demonstrating its effectiveness in enhancing renewable energy utilization and economic efficiency.

articleTitle: Skin Disease Identification and Skincare Solutions Using Deep Learning Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Integrated Intelligence and Communication Systems (ICIICS)
abstract: The major challenge in dermatology is the accurate diagnosis and treatment of skin disorders. This issue can be addressed by using advanced machine-learning techniques.
