In this paper, we propose a hybrid deep-learning architecture consisting of Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) and Support Vector Machines (SVM) for predicting skin diseases more accurately in an automated way. By analyzing the input image of the diseased skin, the AI-based prediction system offers timely medical interventions and supports doctors in making well-informed treatment decisions. Achieving a prediction accuracy of 95.09 %, the proposed ensemble model is capable of detecting various skin diseases and also is designed to provide personalized skincare recommendations. Further, we have designed a user-friendly application that integrates seamlessly into existing healthcare systems and ensures data privacy and security in compliance with strict regulations. The proposed diagnostic platform aims to revolutionize dermatological care, making diagnosis and treatment more efficient and leading to improved patient outcomes.

articleTitle: A Hybrid LSTM-GAN Model for Predictive Cyber Threat Intelligence and Anomaly Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Integrated Intelligence and Communication Systems (ICIICS)
abstract: Cybersecurity is increasingly challenged by complex and evolving threats that require predictive intelligence and advanced anomaly detection. This paper presents a novel Hybrid LSTM-GAN (Long Short-Term Memory - Generative Adversarial Network) model designed for predictive cyber threat intelligence and real-time anomaly detection. By leveraging LSTM's ability to capture temporal dependencies in sequential data and GAN's strength in generating synthetic samples, this hybrid model enhances the detection of subtle and emerging cyber threats. The model first uses LSTM layers to analyze patterns within time-series data, identifying potential anomalies. A GAN is then employed to generate realistic threat scenarios, enhancing the model's ability to recognize unusual activity and improve generalization. This two-step approach is crucial for capturing complex patterns and reducing false positives, which are common in conventional detection methods. Experimental results on benchmark cybersecurity datasets demonstrate that the proposed model achieves a 92.5% detection accuracy, a 15% reduction in false positives compared to standalone LSTM models, and a 25% improvement in threat prediction capabilities over traditional methods. These values indicate that the Hybrid LSTM-GAN model is a powerful tool for predictive threat intelligence, providing proactive and reliable anomaly detection across various cybersecurity applications.

articleTitle: A Smart Traffic Flow Optimization Using Graph Convolutional Network with Graph Long Short-Term Memory
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Integrated Intelligence and Communication Systems (ICIICS)
abstract: In recent years, Smart Cities (SC), Traffic Flow (TF) refers to the optimized movement of vehicles, pedestrians, and other road users by progressive technologies. Predicting traffic flow is dynamic to ease congestion, enhance traffic management, and to improve emergency response. Previously, many methods were proposed to enhance the prediction of traffic flow, although the existing methods have overfitting, computational complexity, and generalizability problems. To overcome these problems, a Graph Convolutional Network based Graph Long Short-Term Memory (GCN-GLSTM) model is considered to predict traffic flow. Initially, Urban Traffic Density in Cities (UTDC) dataset is employed to optimize the flow of traffic. The preprocessing is performed with Data cleaning, to remove outliers and missing values, Data filtering to remove data points with low GPS accuracy, Z-Score normalization to normalize data, and Data transformation to Converted data into suitable formats. Feature extraction is performed by employing Graph Attention Network (GAN) to handle complexity. For classification, GCN-GLSTM is used to handle high-dimensionality, and to enhance generalizability. The proposed GCN-GLSTM method gained high performance metrics such as accuracy, MSE, MAE, and RMSE of 98.34%, 1.72, 1.14, and 1.35 compared to existing methods like Graph Neural Network (GNN).

Author Keywords: graph convolutional network with graph long short-term memory

articleTitle: An Effective Personality Prediction Using Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers with AdamW Optimizer
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Integrated Intelligence and Communication Systems (ICIICS)
abstract: In recent days, each and every individual personality reflects the individual behavior of person. Therefore, it is essential to assess the personality that enhances the behavior of individuals across the world. Previous researchers have used various machine learning and deep learning analyzes individuals' traits across psychology, human resources, marketing, and mental health. However, predicting personality is challenging due to the subjective nature of traits, ethical considerations around data privacy, and the need for models that work accurately across diverse backgrounds. This study suggests a novel approach to develop a deep learning model that resolves these challenges by combining various techniques such as Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (BERT), AdamW Optimizer (BERT-AdamW). Initially, the data is collected from the Myers-Briggs Type Indicator (MBTI) dataset. Further, the data is preprocessed using lowercasing, lemmatization, and stemming and processed through a pre-trained language model namely BERT for feature extraction of optimal features. In addition, the AdamW optimizer is utilized to enhance the performance of BERT and finally LR model is incorporated to predict the personality behavior of an individual. The BERT-AdamW model resulted with 97.89% accuracy when compared with Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM).

articleTitle: Effective Diabetes Mellitus Prediction Using a Hybrid Ensemble Machine Learning Model with Iot
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Integrated Intelligence and Communication Systems (ICIICS)
abstract: Demand for healthcare Internet of things (IoT) devices that forecast and track illnesses has been driven by the rising worldwide prevalence of diabetes, which impacts more than 346 million people. A healthcare approach that does not involve invasive IoT monitoring and uses machine learning to forecast the likelihood of diabetes from key indicators like blood glucose levels is proposed in this study. The major objective is to create a program that assists diabetics in keeping their condition under control. Predicting the consequences of diabetes, the algorithm achieves 98.41 percent accuracy by using machine learning techniques, particularly bagging and boosting. For the purpose of training the model, 10, 221 users' data was culled from the PIMA database (PID), questionnaires, and IoT sensors. The IoT app provided a superior solution for predicting diabetes risk variables by integrating three conventional machine learning methods with a hybrid ensemble approach. This allowed it to outperform previous models.

articleTitle: AI-Powered Multi View Face Video Super-Resolution Techniques for Real-Time Video Processing
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Integrated Intelligence and Communication Systems (ICIICS)
abstract: In order to improve the visual quality of low-resolution video frames, this study introduces a new super-resolution method for real-time video processing that is powered by artificial intelligence. With little computational overhead, the suggested approach uses a hybrid deep learning model to reconstruct high-resolution frames. This model mixes Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) with Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs). The suggested method outperforms state-of-the-art methods by 12.3% in PSNR and 8.7% in SSIM, according to experimental results on benchmark video datasets. The PSNR is 34.56 dB and the SSIM is 0.94. Also, running on a GTX 1080Ti GPU, the system shows an average processing speed of 30 fps, which is great for real-time apps. The suggested strategy is effective in eliminating artifacts, improving visual clarity, and retaining fine details in various real-time video processing contexts, according to both quantitative and qualitative results.

articleTitle: Efficient Classification of Rotten and Healthy Bell Peppers Using an Optimized DenseNet121 Model
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Integrated Intelligence and Communication Systems (ICIICS)
abstract: In the countries like India with the growing population and rising food demands, agriculture, cold storage and transportation process plays a critical role in the country, highlighting the need to maximize crop yields and food preservation. Bell pepper cultivation and classification of rotten and healthy bell peppers during preservation in cold storage and transportation process is severely affected by the deterioration of produce, which results in substantial financial losses. To minimize wastage and ensure the quality of produce, timely and accurate classification of rotten versus healthy bell peppers is important. With the rise of computer vision and machine learning, automated classification systems offer a promising solution. The study proposes a novel deep-learning method for effectively classifying rotten bell peppers and healthy bell peppers using the optimized DenseNet121 model, which enhances the accuracy of classification. Due to the optimized DenseNet121 model's exceptional performance in feature extraction and classification, it offers a practical solution that can be utilized not only in cultivation fields but also in storage areas where bell peppers are kept before they are sent to factories. This can substantially improve the process of sorting, reducing post-harvest losses, and supporting productivity in agriculture by ensuring only high-quality supply moves further along the supply chain. Experimental results show that the DenseNet121 model achieves a remarkable 98.81% accuracy in distinguishing healthy and rotten bell peppers.

articleTitle: Integrating Quantum Metaheuristics with Stackelberg Game and Auction Mechanism for Cooperative Data Clustering in Adhoc Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Integrated Intelligence and Communication Systems (ICIICS)
abstract: Data clustering in adhoc networks is challenging due to their dynamic and decentralised nature. Traditional methods often struggle to adapt to the constant changes in such environments. This paper introduces a novel approach that com-bines game theory with Quantum Particle Swarm Optimisation (QPSO) to enhance resource utilisation, network stability, and clustering accuracy. In this setup, leader nodes employ QPSO, a faster and more accurate optimization method, to predict follower node responses and develop optimal clustering strategies. Follower nodes then participate in an auction-based resource allocation system, where bids are ranked based on resource needs, energy levels, and connectivity. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed framework outperforms traditional methods, achieving a 25% improvement in clustering efficiency, 30% better inter-cluster separation, and a 20% increase in fairness in resource allocation. This study highlights the potential of integrating game theory, auction mechanisms, and QPSO to achieve more effective and adaptable clustering solutions in dynamic network environments.

articleTitle: Combined Time Series Prediction Model for Multi-Source Data Based on ARIMA-LSTM
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Integrated Intelligence and Communication Systems (ICIICS)
abstract: In this paper, temperature trend assessment and prediction in different climatic zones will be carried out with the help of Pettitt's test, LSTM, and ARIMA. Pettitt's test was conducted for the southern and northern temperate zones as well as for the tropics in establishing the temperature mutation points between 1885 and March 2022. The points of mutation detected had 2008 for the southern temperate zone, 2009 for the northern temperate zone, and 2007 and 2008 for the tropics; hence, it did not tally with the expected mutation in March 2022 that led to the rejection of that claim. Based on the performed LSTM and ARIMA temperature prediction, it was shown that the former provided a result of 14.388°C by 2050 and 14.2048°C by 2100, while the latter returned 14.95°C by 2050 and 15.25°C by 2100. None of these models showed that the temperature would rise to 20°C over the next century. This would put it in 2898 according to ARIMA. It also showed, because of the lack of enough data to train it, the LSTM was overfitted, thus making the ARIMA the more reliable model under this circumstance.

articleTitle: Evaluating Generative Adversarial Networks Performance in Image Synthesis with Graphical Analysis of Loss Functions and Quality Metrics
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Integrated Intelligence and Communication Systems (ICIICS)
abstract: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) have revolutionized image synthesis by using two neural networks, a generator and a discriminator, to create realistic images from random noise. In this adversarial process, the generator attempts to fool the discriminator, which distinguishes between real and fake images. Advanced variants like conditional GANs and CycleGANs enable tasks like specified image generation and style transfer. Our paper presents improvements in image quality and training stability for GANs by introducing new training methods and loss function modifications to address issues like mode collapse. Evaluated on CelebA and CIFAR-10, our model outperforms previous GANs with Inception Scores of 9.69 and 10.79 and Frechet Inception Distances of 7.91 and -9.69, respectively. These results demonstrate better convergence, more stable training, and higher-quality image generation, establishing a new benchmark for GAN research and applications.

articleTitle: Enhanced Deep Learning Model for Pneumonia Segmentation in Chest X-Ray Images
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Integrated Intelligence and Communication Systems (ICIICS)
abstract: Pneumonia from images of chest X-rays requires accurate segmentation for effective diagnosis and treatment. This study proposes an enhanced deep learning model, EASUNet, designed to integrate the EfficientNet-B4 backbone, Atrous Spatial Pyramid Pooling (ASPP) and a U-Net decoder with attention mechanisms to refine segmentation accuracy. The methodology preprocesses ChestX-ray14 data, uses the EfficientNet-B4 backbone for capturing hierarchical features, ASPP module to focus on different scales and contexts in the X-ray images and the U-Net decoder, augmented with attention mechanisms to prioritize relevant features and suppress irrelevant areas improving the model's focus on pneumonia-affected regions. Comparative results show that EASU-Net outperforms traditional models like U-Net, Attention U-Net and DeepLabV3 by achieving a Dice Coefficient of 0.93, accuracy of 95%, and Intersection over Union (IoU) of 0.88. The results suggest that EASU-Net is a reliable segmentation tool, providing medical professionals with improved precision for diagnosing pneumonia from chest X-rays.

articleTitle: Automated Audit Methods Supported by Blockchain Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Integrated Intelligence and Communication Systems (ICIICS)
abstract: With the rapid development of information technology, especially the widespread application of blockchain technology in various industries, the auditing industry is facing challenges and opportunities in the integration of traditional methods and modern technology. This study aims to explore how blockchain technology can enhance data transparency and security in automated auditing, thereby improving audit efficiency and reducing human errors. This study adopts the distributed ledger feature of blockchain to store audit evidence, ensuring that data is tamper proof and easy to trace, and automatically executes standard audit tasks through smart contracts, such as verifying the consistency and integrity of financial statements. The total number of transactions gradually increased from 10000 in January to 16500 in December, indicating that the system's processing power has strengthened over time. The value of this study lies in providing a new technological solution for the auditing industry, and provide theoretical and practical support for promoting the application of blockchain technology in the auditing field.

articleTitle: Comprehensive Analysis of Flood Risk Using Regression Models and Interpretable Machine Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Integrated Intelligence and Communication Systems (ICIICS)
abstract: Since flooding incidences are becoming more frequent and serious globally due to climate change, flood prediction has become more crucial than ever. Recently, in forecasting systems, Machine Learning (ML) is being utilized to build efficient and accurate systems. In this work, ML algorithms Linear, Ridge, Lasso, Polynomial, Support Vector, Decision Tree, Random Forest, Gradient Boosting, and Bayesian Ridge Regression (BRR) are trained using publicly available flood prediction dataset and investigated for their effectiveness. The performance of each model is measured using MSE, RMSE, MAE, and R-squared (R2). Out of all the models, BRR shows the best performance with an R2 value of 1.00. Using the techniques of Explainable AI, namely LIME and SHAP, we further elucidate the model to help obtain greater transparency and reliability of results in predictions
